title: Timeline of the Border
summary: Chronological record of forty key events shaping the Border, listed from the earliest founding compacts to the present crisis.

head: Year
Event
rows: First Watch masons sink seven meteoric Anchor Seals into the caldera floor to bleed primordial magma pressure away from the upper provinces.
The Crown of Order is forged from fallen star-iron and quenched in alpine snow, binding the First Sovereign to Thornvael's tectonic stability.
Dwarven smith-clans and northern border lords sign the First Compact in iron and tallow, establishing the Undervault drainage galleries.
Twelve primeval quartz wardstones are raised across the Redmarsh plateau to anchor coastal rain-clouds and pin alkali dust below the passes.
Third-Dynasty inland-sea magistrates codify Probate Debt Law, ruling that unpaid granary and tax liens remain enforceable after death.
Imperial masons complete Alder Bridge using Craghorn granite and slaked lime, opening the sole heavy artillery artery to the northern moors.
Geo-sorcerers of the Age of Chains bind living bedrock into Elder Juggernauts to guard mountain passes without wages or rations.
The inland sea evaporates following a southern fault-shift, leaving behind the Redmarsh salt-pans and stranding Third-Dynasty port vaults.
Oakhaven's merchant guild secures the Whale-Oil Charter, financing Harborwatch's great lighthouse and boom-chain fortifications.
Three northern kings refuse to pay the caldera maintenance tithe and are beheaded at the Threshold crossroads, where their headless statues still stand.
Expelled scholars from the Capital Collegium publish the first treatise on Arcane Thermodynamics, proving invocations act as pressure valves.
Exiled dwarven engineers seal the lower Undervault inspection shafts with lead after northern bailiffs use the tunnels to hide clipped silver.
The Lantern-Keeper hermit order strings iron-caged oil beacons through Lantern Passage to guide caravans around the deepest fen sinks.
Deep Quarry prison gangs cut three hundred feet into black ironstone seams before striking an underground spring that floods the lowest gallery.
Arch-Mage Malrik trades his sight to read subterranean magma veins, sparking the Caldera Schism as half the Crown College follows him south.
Brother Elias and surviving Collegium archivists don iron collars, founding the Scorched Penitents to guard against unbinding the Anchor Seals.
High Quartermaster Morvessa drafts the emergency Salt Tithe, stripping border parishes of brine, grain, and iron ore to fund southern forts.
Thornwick's Border Mint is burned to the ground after Assayer Pell uncovers shaved silver groats stamped with worn commission dies.
Ashen Coven sorcerers under Mordred and Hexer Saelen establish secret blood-altars in the Sunken Sanctum and Redmarsh willow hollows.
Gorrathul's engineers conceal the silting of Ironheart Bastion's lower water cisterns while conscripting miners to fortify the mountain pass.
Lord Admiral Vesperion assembles the Black Fleet of copper-sheeted war galleys to blockade Oakhaven and sever coastal supply routes.
0 (Spring Thaw)
Grok'tar's gnoll warband massacres the Thornwick night-watch at Sunken Ford, burning the tollhouse to destroy forged Border Mint dispatches.
0 (Day 4)
Vanguard survivors rally at Thornwick Market and clear marsh-wisps and Coven scouts from the rotting boardwalks of Fenwick's fen.
0 (Day 9)
Four treacherous pickets pull the iron stakes at Ravenwatch Tower, forcing defenders into the Weeping Ossuary beneath the keep.
The vanguard breaks Morvessa's silk-webbed brood-nest beneath Ravenwatch and recovers stolen border tax-ledgers.
Pikemen hold Alder Bridge through three raider assaults while three thousand river-parish refugees evacuate south toward Redmarsh.
Commander Velen's siege-rams shatter Ashbrook Gatehouse; defenders burn the manor granary and retreat across the southern border ditch.
0 (Month 2)
Blood-chanters crack three quartz wardstones on the Plateau, unleashing static storms and red alkali grit across Bracken Basin.
0 (Month 2, Wk 3)
Chained ironstone miners revolt during the vanguard assault on Deep Quarry, flooding the lower terraces and starving Ironheart's forges.
0 (Month 3)
The vanguard storms Ironheart Bastion and slays Gorrathul, discovering its legendary cisterns had silted dry years earlier.
0 (Month 3, Wk 4)
Mercenaries swear the Bailey Truce at Oakhaven, securing whale-oil casks and armory access in exchange for clearing the sea-gate.
0 (Month 4)
The vanguard wades the rising surf to breach the Sunken Citadel and rescues stranded soldiers off the flooding Hourglass Spit.
0 (Month 4, Wk 3)
Vesperion's fire-hulks torch Harborwatch's timber quays, but reclaimed seawall culverins shatter his flagship and break the blockade.
0 (Month 5)
Crossing to the volcanic coast, the vanguard links up with Forgemaster Vok's smiths in Ironcamp and marches onto the basalt highway.
0 (Month 5, Wk 2)
Turncoat watchmen extinguish the hilltop signal beacons along the foothills before vanguard scouts purge the traitors' garrison.
0 (Month 5, Wk 4)
Arch-Mage Malrik flees Ironcamp with stolen cipher-keys, falling on the Ashveil summit portal stairs before he can seal the inner rift.
0 (Month 6)
Assault columns breach the Gauntlet of Iron and Greystone's outer rampart, driving Ember Court forces back behind the magma moat.
0 (Month 6, Wk 2)
Vanguard defenders defeat three converging relief armies in detail at Three-Roads Watch, isolating the Infernal Citadel.
0 (Month 6, Wk 3)
At the Crossroads of Headless Kings, the liberators choose their path and march down the Colonnade of Conquered Crowns.
0 (Solstice)
The last Anchor Seals fracture on the Obsidian Dais; Ashkarath falls, leaving Thornvael's fate balanced between cold starlight and living ember.

p: History on the Border is rarely written by poets; it is pieced together from water-damaged tax rolls, chipped boundary stones, and tavern arguments. Read from oldest to newest, these forty entries trace how a quiet frontier slowly caught fire.

title: The Border Fords Wardens
summary: Remnants of Thornwick's provincial levy and bridge-pickets who held the Alder River crossings after the Salt Tithe stripped their armories. Stubborn, mud-stained pragmatists who value dry powder, honest weight, and unbroken watch-rotations above noble titles.
infobox: Mire-Runner, Picket-Bearer, Bridge-Warden, Ford-Marshal, Keeper of the Alder

p: Remnants of Thornwick's provincial levy and bridge-pickets who held the Alder River crossings after the Salt Tithe stripped their armories. Stubborn, mud-stained pragmatists who value dry powder, honest weight, and unbroken watch-rotations above noble titles.

list: Hostile: Keep your hand off your hilt—every sentry on the Alder has orders to drop you on sight.
Wary: We know your face from the toll-rolls, stranger. State your business and keep moving.
Neutral: The mud doesn't care who wears the crown, and neither do we. Pay your toll and pass.
Friendly: Good to see dry steel at the gate. Quartermaster left extra bolts by the brazier for you.
Honored: When the river rose red, you stood on the planks with us. Every ford in the north is yours.

title: Redmarsh Salt-Caravaneers
summary: Guild of alkali-haulers, cistern-guards, and dune-scouts keeping trade moving across the evaporated inland sea. Bound by strict water-sharing oaths, they despise both Morvessa's tax-bailiffs and Sand-Clan ambushers who bleed their supply trains.
infobox: Water-Bearer, Axle-Guard, Dune-Outrider, Caravan-Factor, Master of the Salt-Road

p: Guild of alkali-haulers, cistern-guards, and dune-scouts keeping trade moving across the evaporated inland sea. Bound by strict water-sharing oaths, they despise both Morvessa's tax-bailiffs and Sand-Clan ambushers who bleed their supply trains.

list: Hostile: Not a drop of water or a pinch of salt for thieves—ride back into the alkali dust.
Wary: Keep clear of the lead wagons until the outriders check your saddlebags for tax-badges.
Neutral: Silver buys hardbread and boiled brine; trouble buys an arrow from the canyon rim.
Friendly: You cleared the corduroy road when our axles sank. Draw from the clean cask at half price.
Honored: Your name is carved on every milestone well from Redmarsh to the pass. Ride at our head.

title: The Lower-Parish Scriptorium
summary: Order of mortuary clerks, probate notarists, and debt-wardens descended from Third-Dynasty inland-sea magistrates. They treat necromancy as cold legal accounting, binding unquiet spirits only until every witnessed oath and unpaid lien is settled.
infobox: Tallow-Clerk, Lien-Notary, Crypt-Bailiff, Probate-Arbiter, Grand Seal-Keeper

p: Order of mortuary clerks, probate notarists, and debt-wardens descended from Third-Dynasty inland-sea magistrates. They treat necromancy as cold legal accounting, binding unquiet spirits only until every witnessed oath and unpaid lien is settled.

list: Hostile: Your name is entered in red gall-ink; even death will not discharge what you owe this parish.
Wary: Touch nothing on the probate shelves unless you carry a witnessed writ of inheritance.
Neutral: Every soul owes a final ledger-balance. Keep your accounts current and we have no quarrel.
Friendly: Your field audits saved three crypt vaults from grave-robbers. The archives are open to you.
Honored: By seal and tallow, your debts are forgiven in perpetuity, and our witnesses answer your call.

title: Oakhaven Maritime Guild
summary: Shipwrights, lighthouse keepers, and culverin-masters governing the walled hill-city where the Greywash meets the sea. Shrewd tariff-collectors who hoarded whale-oil behind bolted gates until Vesperion's blockade forced them to arm mercenaries.
infobox: Dock-Hand, Boom-Warden, Harbor-Pilot, Sea-Wall Captain, Admiral of the Mole

p: Shipwrights, lighthouse keepers, and culverin-masters governing the walled hill-city where the Greywash meets the sea. Shrewd tariff-collectors who hoarded whale-oil behind bolted gates until Vesperion's blockade forced them to arm mercenaries.

list: Hostile: The harbor chains stay raised against pirates and traitors—turn back before the culverins fire.
Wary: Guild curfew bells ring at dusk. Keep to the lower piers and stay away from the drydocks.
Neutral: Pay the anchorage tariff in weighed coin and Oakhaven's chandlers will fit your company.
Friendly: You broke the fire-hulks off the outer mole. Our shipwrights will temper your steel free of charge.
Honored: The lighthouse burns in your honor tonight; every keel in Oakhaven sails at your command.

title: The Thermodynamic Conclave
summary: Dissident scholars and mint-assayers expelled from the Capital Collegium for proving that invocation magic obeys strict pressure and grounding laws. Armed with copper wire and quartz lenses, they repair ruptured wardstones while mocking priestly liturgy.
infobox: Copper-Winder, Bench-Assayer, Ward-Surveyor, Conclave-Fellow, High Thermodynamicist

p: Dissident scholars and mint-assayers expelled from the Capital Collegium for proving that invocation magic obeys strict pressure and grounding laws. Armed with copper wire and quartz lenses, they repair ruptured wardstones while mocking priestly liturgy.

list: Hostile: Sloppy grounding and worse manners—get out of our laboratory before you short the wardstones.
Wary: Mind where you set your iron boots; that chalk circle is calibrated to three decimal grains.
Neutral: Bring intact quartz prisms or copper filings and we will trade you properly grounded runes.
Friendly: Your field readings from the plateau proved our pressure thesis. Take a calibrated focus.
Honored: You understand that magic is pure law, not superstition. The Conclave's vaults belong to you.

title: The Ironcamp Slag-Guild
summary: Keloid-scarred weaponsmiths, siege-sappers, and quarry-liberators working the volcanic foothills beside the Ember border. Led by Forgemaster Vok, they quench meteoric star-iron in open caldera fissures to arm anyone bold enough to storm the throne.
infobox: Bellows-Puller, Slag-Quencher, Anvil-Striker, Siege-Sapper, Master of the Fissure

p: Keloid-scarred weaponsmiths, siege-sappers, and quarry-liberators working the volcanic foothills beside the Ember border. Led by Forgemaster Vok, they quench meteoric star-iron in open caldera fissures to arm anyone bold enough to storm the throne.

list: Hostile: Step near the quenching troughs and we will hammer you flat like bad bog-iron.
Wary: Put on smoked goggles and keep your hands off the meteoric billets until Vok speaks for you.
Neutral: Bring clean star-iron or sulfur brine and our trip-hammers will turn out honest steel.
Friendly: Good temper in your blade and no fear of sparks—the guild will re-forge your plate at cost.
Honored: You stood in the fissure heat when the walls shook. Our finest caldera steel bears your mark.

title: Order of Scorched Penitents
summary: Sightless battle-mages and ash-robed archivists following Brother Elias, wearing heavy iron collars to atone for opening the caldera's first cinder-gates centuries ago. They guard forbidden volcanic lore and tend wounded soldiers on scorched battlefields.

p: Sightless battle-mages and ash-robed archivists following Brother Elias, wearing heavy iron collars to atone for opening the caldera's first cinder-gates centuries ago. They guard forbidden volcanic lore and tend wounded soldiers on scorched battlefields.

list: Hostile: You carry the reek of unbridled ambition—turn back before the ember consumes another fool.
Wary: Speak softly in the cloister; our ears read the tremor of every lie in your boots.
Neutral: We tend the burned and copy the warnings left by the dead. Share water and rest in peace.
Friendly: You showed mercy where others brought torches. Let Brother Elias read the ash-scrolls for you.
Honored: Through soot and trial you have proven worthy of the threshold truth. Walk in our vigil.

title: The First Watch Remnant
summary: Undying spectral wardens and ancestral oath-keepers bound to the seven meteoric Anchor Seals beneath the Obsidian Dais. Stoic, ancient, and terrifyingly literal, they recognize only those who uphold the original compact to keep Thornvael from burning.
infobox: Oath-Witness, Seal-Bearer, Pillar-Warden, Threshold-Arbiter, First Watch Sovereign

p: Undying spectral wardens and ancestral oath-keepers bound to the seven meteoric Anchor Seals beneath the Obsidian Dais. Stoic, ancient, and terrifyingly literal, they recognize only those who uphold the original compact to keep Thornvael from burning.

list: Hostile: Oath-breakers find no mercy on the obsidian steps—only cold iron and endless watch.
Wary: The seals hum uneasily at your approach. Prove your discipline before touching the valves.
Neutral: Seven seals hold the mountain's wrath. State your purpose and respect the ancient boundary.
Friendly: You mended what traitors fractured. The pillars recognize a true defender of the soil.
Honored: By star-iron and unbroken vow, the First Watch salutes its rightful commander at the Threshold.

title: Alder Ford Toll Daybook
summary: Act I lore book written by Toll-Clerk Brann, recovered during Blood at the Ford to shed light on border trade.

p: Fourteen salt-wagons passed south before the thaw flooded the gravel bar, each paying three copper pence and a signed tallow chit from Morvessa's bailiffs. By dusk the river rose two cubits, carrying dead sheep and broken alder poles out of Greywood. Sergeant Garrick ordered the chain raised at compline, yet the relief riders from Thornwick never blew their horn. Half the ink on this page is smeared by river spray; the rest is a tally of crossbow quarrels we never received.

Rainwater has blurred the margin totals, yet Brann's cramped handwriting still tracks every grain-cart, sheep-drove, and sealed imperial wagon that crossed the Alder shallows. The final page breaks off mid-sentence beside a dark smudge.

title: Peat-Cutter's Warning
summary: Act I lore book authored by Foreman Odo, discovered in Whispers in the Fen regarding the maintenance of bog crossings.

p: Whoever takes the east plank-walk after sundown must keep his lantern shuttered to a slit and count the willow-stakes at every bend. Three turf-diggers from Fenwick followed a green marsh-light off the timbers on Tuesday and left nothing behind save two wooden clogs floating upright in black water. The bog remembers every drowning since the First Compact; do not answer when a voice calls your baptismal name from beneath the reeds.

Nailed originally to a rotting cedar post above the peat-ditches, this oilcloth notice warns travelers which planks will hold a mule and which will swallow a man whole. Odo's last line begs Thornwick for whale oil that never came.

title: Ravenwatch Relief Roster
summary: Act I lore book compiled by Corporal Hobb, found during Nightfall at Ravenwatch detailing the garrison's final shifts.

p: Week nine without pay-silver or dry firewood. Four men slipped down the west scree before moonrise, taking the iron-shod pickets from the outer ditch so the gnolls could walk straight up to the timber gate. We have two barrels of pine pitch left and thirty-six bolts between seven bowmen. If the smoke-beacon on Craghorn does not answer tonight, burn the cipher-books in the cellar brazier and bar the trapdoor from below.

A damp vellum roll listing watch-posts, lantern tallies, and four names scratched out twice with an angry iron nib. Hobb kept neat records to the very end, noting with dry bitterness that the relief column was three weeks overdue.

title: Sunken Sanctum Lien-Roll
summary: Act I lore book penned by Brother Anselm, uncovered in The Sunken Sanctum recording posthumous parish debts.

p: Let it be entered into the lower-parish ledger that Miller Tobin died owing forty bushels of winter rye and six silver groats to the Border Tithe. Pursuant to Third-Dynasty probate custom, his corpse has been anointed with gall-ink and bound to the north pier until his labor satisfies the arrears. Groundwater now stands ankle-deep in the scriptorium; the damp rots our vellum faster than the dead can pay off their interest.

Bound in mildewed calfskin and weighted with lead corners so it would not float away when the lower crypts flooded. Inside, Anselm meticulously logs every unpaid tithe, funeral fee, and lien carried past the grave.

title: Lantern-Keeper's Almanac
summary: Act I lore book kept by Keeper Soren, found in Lantern Passage chronicling oil rations and fog-watch shifts.

p: A gill of whale-oil burns four hours in dry air, three in canyon mist, and barely one when things from the slate cliffs breathe against the iron cage. For forty winters my order has trimmed the wicks along Lantern Passage so supply trains need not risk the bottomless peat sinks. Tonight the third lamp burned bright blue without a breath of wind, and something heavy scraped four-toed claws across the limestone roof above my hut.

Page after page of quiet, obsessive measurements: drops of whale oil burned per hour, wind direction off the fen, and the exact night the supply runners stopped answering his horn. Soren trusted his lanterns more than any lord.

title: Sawmill Haulage Manifest
summary: Act I lore book written by Factor Merrick, discovered in Greywood Supply detailing timber quotas and mill haulage.

p: Stacked beneath the south shed: ninety seasoned oak planks for Oakhaven drydocks, forty ash spear-shafts, and twelve casks of pine resin. Our draft-oxen were hamstrung at dawn by irregulars wearing Morvessa's brass tax-badges on bloodied coats. We wedged the water-wheel with iron crowbars before fleeing toward Thornwick; let the timber rot in the sawdust before the Salt-Tithe Commission hauls a single beam south.

Scratched onto hinged slate tablets wrapped in waxed twine to survive sawmill sawdust and autumn sleet. Merrick's figures show oak beams vanishing south by the hundred while Thornwick's own palisade rotted in the mud.

title: Split Column Dispatch
summary: Act I lore book drafted by Captain Velen's Adjutant, found in Split Vanguard outlining troop movements along the border.

p: By order of the Southern Bailiwick, the first column will force the limestone defile while outriders sweep the west gully to cut off Thornwick's scouts. Take no prisoners from the border levy; their magistrates forfeited crown protection when they withheld the autumn iron-tithe. Burn every granary and mill-weir along the Alder so the northern parishes must beg Redmarsh for salt and bread by midwinter.

Crisp military shorthand stamped with Southern Crown wax, ordering forced marches without baggage trains or proper winter boots. Even the adjutant's neat script betrays quiet unease over how thin the northern line was stretched.

title: Alder Bridge Survey Notes
summary: Act I lore book recorded by Master Mason Dorin, uncovered at Alder Bridge describing the ancient span's construction.

p: Built in the forty-second year of the First Compact from dressed Craghorn granite and mortared with slaked lime and ox-blood. Three arches span the main channel, each keyed to bear twelve-ton siege culverins without settling. Should northern commanders ever need to deny the crossing, pack black powder into the hollow pier-chambers behind the western cutwater and fire the fuse from the chalk bluff.

Copied from a weathered bronze survey plate bolted beneath the central arch. Dorin boasted that his three-arched stonework would outlast every king in the South, provided nobody was foolish enough to undermine the ley-piers.

title: Ironhide Spoor Notes
summary: Act I lore book kept by Huntsman Corvus, found during Ironhide Hunt tracking the movements of Greywood beasts.

p: Tracked the great greywood tusk-beast three leagues through bramble thickets after it snapped two steel leg-traps and gored three hounds. Its hide is matted with dried river-clay and broken iron spear-heads that have healed straight into its shoulders. Ordinary broadheads glance harmlessly off the ridge of its spine; only a heavy ash-boar spear planted squarely under the left foreleg will reach its heart.

Stained with pine resin and dried mud, these folded sheets map thorn-boar wallows, broken snares, and strange tracks near the old quarry. Corvus noted that the woodland beasts stopped fleeing human scent weeks before the raids began.

title: Undervault Drainage Writ
summary: Act I lore book issued by Dwarven Factor Thrain, recovered in Undervault Links detailing the subterranean drainage tunnels.

p: Notice to Border Magistrates: the granite sluice-gates beneath Gallery Four hold back the spring melt from the northern ridge. Three hundred years ago your forefathers swore in iron and tallow to keep the drainage channels clear of silt. Now your tax-clerks have bricked up the inspection shafts to hide confiscated silver, and cold pressure builds behind the lead-sealed doors like a drumhead ready to burst.

Written in blunt, practical prose that wastes no ink on pleasantries. Thrain warns the human magistrates that sealing the lead drainage galleries to hide smuggling caches will eventually flood the entire southern approach.

title: Unsent Letter from Ashbrook
summary: Act I lore book written by Stewardess Marta, found during Ashbrook Retreat capturing the final hours before evacuation.

p: Dearest Sister in Oakhaven, the turnip fields are full of ash and freshly turned earth. Velen's rams broke the outer gatehouse before dawn, and our own levies burned the granary so the bailiffs could not take it. We are packing the silver candlesticks and the parish birth-rolls into two handcarts to follow the pikemen south into Redmarsh. Pray the wardstones still hold the dust back when we reach the plateau.

Folded neatly and addressed to a sister in Oakhaven, yet never handed to a courier. Marta describes packing silver candlesticks into grain sacks while ash drifted over the southern ridge for the first time in living memory.

title: Thornwick Curfew Decree
summary: Act I lore book proclaimed by Bailiff Harken, located in Thornwick Market setting curfew and rationing rules.

p: By authority of the Market Council, all town gates close at the second evening bell. Drovers arriving after dark must stable their beasts outside the palisade and pay double lantern-tax at dawn. Any citizen caught hoarding salt-fish, smelting scrap iron without a mint stamp, or speaking with hooded strangers from the Sunken Sanctum shall forfeit his stall and serve thirty days digging moat-ditches.

Posted beside the tavern door where half the town could read it and the other half could spit on it. Harken's decree forbids hoarding tallow, carrying unsheathed axes after dusk, or spreading rumors about the Salt Tithe.

title: Clipped Coin Investigation
summary: Act I lore book compiled by Assayer Pell, discovered at the Border Mint Ruins exposing debased coinage.

p: Tested forty silver groats seized from Morvessa's tax-wagons: every single coin was shaved three grains light and re-struck with a worn Border Mint die. The missing silver was melted into unmarked bars and hauled south toward Redmarsh under cover of night. When I threatened to send my assay scales to the Capital Collegium, two bailiffs barred the furnace doors and set fire to the roof beams. The charcoal dregs still smell of sulfur and tallow.

Hidden beneath a cracked crucible, Pell's private assay notes prove that fresh copper slugs were being struck underweight by order from above. Every column ends with the same grim question: where was the real silver going?

title: Waterlogged Courier Tube
summary: Act I lore book scribbled by Scout Fenwick, salvaged from the Thornwick Weir inside a sealed tube.

p: Recovered from a dead rider wedged in the willow eel-weir: Grok'tar's gnoll warband did not raid Sunken Ford for plunder. They were paid in stamped Border Mint copper to slaughter the night-watch and burn the tollhouse ledgers before auditors arrived from the coast. If this tube reaches Thornwick, warn Sergeant Garrick that the enemy is already inside the tax-commission. Wet mud cakes the brass seal.

A soaked, frantic scrap of parchment stuffed into a waxed reed-case before Fenwick had to swim the flooded eel-weirs. Half the ink has run, leaving only hurried warnings about gnoll scouts carrying southern copper.

title: Vitrified Slag Observations
summary: Act I lore book penned by Alchemist Toren, found at the Vitrified Kilns studying strange green furnace slag.

p: When bog-iron ore is smelted with crushed river-quartz and peat-charcoal at extreme draft, the waste slag cools into translucent green glass harder than cold chisel-steel. Local miners discard it in heaps behind the old kilns, yet shards bound to ash-wood staves conduct static lightning far cleaner than raw copper. Someone has been digging through our waste pits by lantern-light every new moon. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Toren's careful sketches document how intense arcane heat turned ordinary Greywood brick and melted bronze into humming green glass. His final margin note warns that local wolves have started sleeping beside the warm slag-heaps.

title: Stockade Water-Ration Log
summary: Act II lore book maintained by Quartermaster Bram, found in Redmarsh Outpost tracking scarce water rations.

p: Half a pint of boiled rainwater per man at sunrise, a gill of bitter vinegar-brine at dusk. The moat water turns leather boots green within three days and rots any scratch into weeping salt-ulcers. Caravan drivers arriving from the south claim three of the plateau wardstones have gone dark, and red alkali grit is already blowing north across the corduroy road. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Every tin dipper of boiled vinegar-brine is accounted for down to the half-gill, signed with thumbprints by thirsty drovers and soldiers alike. Bram's ledger reads less like a supply book and more like a countdown.

title: Ochre Ditch Survey
summary: Act II lore book authored by Surveyor Lyra, discovered in Redmarsh Border mapping the shifting alkali ditches.

p: Every iron boundary post sunk into the Redmarsh border tilts three degrees east each winter as the underlying salt-pan dissolves. Yesterday our chain-crew found willow poles hung with bleached sheep-skulls marking a hidden dry path straight through the sucking bog—placed not by royal engineers, but by Sand-Clan outriders guiding contraband iron wagons around our stockade. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Lyra's dry, precise field notes record how the Ochre Ditch creeps three yards wider every dry season, swallowing old cedar road-markers whole. She writes with quiet anger about caravans ignoring her stakes and losing wagons to the brine.

title: Canyon Crossfire Report
summary: Act II lore book filed by Sergeant Kael, recovered in Twin Passes detailing canyon crossfire tactics.

p: Never split a supply column across both ledges of Twin Passes without clearing the middle spire first. Sand-Clan marksmen wedged behind the sandstone chimneys can drop hornbow shafts onto either track while rolling boulders down the scree. We lost six pack-mules and two chests of minted pay-silver before our archers climbed the sinkhole rim. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

A terse military after-action report scribbled on the back of a supply chit while pinned behind a sandstone boulder. Kael maps the exact blind spots of the chimney-spire snipers so the next column might actually make it through.

title: Blood-Stained Signal Code
summary: Act II lore book written by Outrider Joren, found in Scattered Scouts containing field signal codes.

p: Three short flashes from the east hummock mean dry footing; two long flashes mean dune-lurkers beneath the sand. Our vanguard rode into the tussocks before dawn fog burned off, and the signal mirrors stopped answering one by one. If anyone finds this notebook in the reeds, tell Redmarsh Outpost that the southern road is mined with buried clay firepots. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Darkened at one corner with dried blood and alkali dust, this folded card lists mirror-flashes and horn-blasts used by Redmarsh outriders. Joren's last scrawl warns that the desert raiders have learned to mimic the relief signal.

title: Stockade Timber Ledger
summary: Act II lore book kept by Carpenter Vane, uncovered in Outpost Palisade recording timber and pitch shortages.

p: Drove forty sharpened oak stakes into the eastern mud-ditch today; by tomorrow morning the salt-rot will soften their points like turnips. Conscripts work knee-deep in leech water while raiders snipe from the fog banks. Without fresh pitch from Oakhaven or iron plating from the Deep Quarry, this palisade will not survive another night assault. Three sentries already shiver with marsh-fever. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Vane complains in blunt carpenter's prose that alkali brine eats through fresh cedar pilings in six months flat. Without black bitumen sealant and ironstone brackets, he predicts the whole stockade will tilt into the mud before winter.

title: Wardstone Rupture Notes
summary: Act II lore book written by Scholar Zahra, found during Wardstone Rupture analyzing the failing climate obelisks.

p: The third quartz monolith did not crack from age or lightning. Crimson blood-wards were chiseled directly into its grounding grooves, reversing the harmonic lattice that pins Redmarsh's alkali storms below the passes. Static discharge now arcs three paces from the fractured crystal, and hot red dust is already drifting north toward the Border Fords. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Filled with crisp diagrams of crystal lattices and grounding wires, Zahra's study proves the quartz monoliths did not crack by accident. Someone deliberately carved reverse runes into their bases to whip the alkali flats into permanent storm.

title: Corduroy Road Waybill
summary: Act II lore book signed by Wagon-Master Durn, recovered in Mire Convoy listing freight along the corduroy road.

p: Six heavy wagons bogged axle-deep where spring floods washed out the log causeway: forty barrels of salt pork, twelve crates of steel crossbow prods, and two sealed coffers of apothecary antivenom. Our draft horses broke their traces when shapes crept out of the reed-walls at midnight. We have circled the wagons and lit our last oil lanterns. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Six wagons of salt-pork, oats, and iron spikes logged neatly before departure—and three crates crossed out in a different hand. Durn's angry margin notes demand to know why half his flour was diverted toward the Deep Quarry.

title: Redmarsh Granary Tally
summary: Act II lore book maintained by Storekeeper Maren, found in Granary Raid detailing Redmarsh's food reserves.

p: Stored above the floodline on limestone stilts: four hundred sacks of winter barley and sixty jars of rendered mutton fat. Smoke is curling up through the floor planks where raiders piled wet brush beneath the piers to smoke us out. We have barred the oak shutters and poured drinking water onto the floorboards to keep the planks from catching. Ash sifts down across the ledger margins. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Maren tallies every sack hoisted up to the limestone stilt-granary, noting weevil losses, brine-damp spoilage, and armed guards posted on the ladders. Reading the totals makes it painfully clear how close the outpost sits to starvation.

title: Saelen's Bog-Curse Formula
summary: Act II lore book written by Hexer Saelen, uncovered in Hexer's Hollow outlining bitter oasis-cursing formulas.

p: Steep three willow-roots in stagnant marsh-brine until the froth turns copper-green, then bind a debtor's knuckle-bone with unbleached linen. When buried beneath a garrison well, the hex sours every drop of water within forty paces and turns minor blisters into gangrene. Let the border lords drink their own unpaid taxes. Never stir the pot with bare iron. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Cramped, spiteful recipes written in green copper-ink on scraps of boiled hide. Saelen details how boiling debtor bones with alkali salts sours a clean aquifer, turning a caravan's last hope into a slow, burning fever.

title: Smuggled Quarry Tally
summary: Act II lore book smuggled out by Miner Gorin, found in Deep Quarry listing chained northern debtors.

p: Three hundred feet below the rim, chained crews cut dense black ironstone by tallow-lamp while rainwater rises around our ankles. Gorrathul's overseers whip any man who slows his pick, yet they refuse to pump the flooded lower gallery because ancient Third-Dynasty doors sit sealed behind the silt. Last night the water level dropped two inches on its own, and something knocked from the dark side of the bronze sluice.

Written with a charred splinter on the inside of a flour sack, this roll names forty-seven Thornwick farmers and smiths worked to the bone in the basalt pits. Gorin's final line is not a plea for mercy, but a count of hidden pickaxes.

title: Blockhouse Siege Journal
summary: Act II lore book kept by Lieutenant Corin, discovered in Lean Garrison chronicling a desperate blockhouse siege.

p: Day thirty-eight since the autumn washout cut our road. Yesterday we boiled the last spare saddle-leathers with wild onions; today we divided twelve crossbow bolts among eight men. A Sand-Clan herald shouted from the ridge that Ironheart's cisterns are full of fresh water if we surrender our banners, yet we can see empty dust-devils blowing straight through their open sluice-gates. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Short, exhausted entries written by tallow stub while sand-raiders prowl outside the shutters. Corin records boiling boot-laces for broth, counting his last twelve crossbow bolts, and listening for a relief horn that takes far too long.

title: Magistrate's Evacuation Order
summary: Act II lore book issued by Magistrate Orin, found in Fleeing Column ordering the civilian evacuation.

p: All inhabitants of the lower salt-parishes are ordered to abandon their homesteads and march north along the raised causeway before dusk. Leave heavy furniture and grain-bins behind; pack only water-skins, winter cloaks, and portable silver. Rear-guard pikemen will hold the stone culverts against dune-raiders until the last handcart clears the marsh border. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Stamped with a cracked municipal seal, Orin's writ commands every family in the upper basins to abandon their carts and march light toward the mountain gates. Even formal legal prose cannot hide the desperation between the lines.

title: Ironheart Water Audit
summary: Act II lore book written by Engineer Vesper, recovered at Fork of Spears measuring the mountain reservoirs.

p: Confidential report to Commander Gorrathul: the eastern and western rock-cisterns beneath Ironheart Bastion have silted completely dry following the Deep Quarry tremor. Our reserves consist solely of forty casks of brackish rainwater—barely six days' supply for the garrison. Recommend immediate withdrawal to the Iron Coast before the vanguard discovers we are defending empty stone. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt.

Cold, undeniable engineering measurements: flow rates, silt depths, and cracked glacier-conduits checked three times over. Vesper's final entry is blunt enough to break a kingdom's heart—the mountain is dead, and only the sea remains.

title: Third-Dynasty Canopic Writ
summary: Act II lore book penned by High Embalmer Seti, found in the Redrock Assay Vault explaining Third-Dynasty burial law.

p: By decree of the Inland Sea Throne, he who dies in arrears to the Royal Granary shall have his viscera sealed in four bitumen jars and his ribs woven with copper wire. Until his kin redeem the tally-tablet in weighed silver, his hollow frame shall patrol the salt-vaults and strike down every thief who breaches the sandstone seal. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Seti explains with dry bureaucratic pride how copper wire, bitumen, and stamped silver tally-tablets bind a debtor's estate cleanly across centuries. To a Third-Dynasty notary, death is merely a change of address, never a pardon.

title: Four-Faced Obelisk Rubbing
summary: Act II lore book compiled by Chronicler Zahra, discovered at the Four-Faced Milestone documenting tampered road signs.

p: The original imperial chiseling on the crossroads milestone reads: 'To Oakhaven Harbor, forty leagues; to the Celestial Spire, ninety leagues.' Someone has hammered out the southern mileage and carved crooked arrows pointing directly toward the deepest alkali sinkholes—a deliberate trap laid to swallow northern relief columns. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Charcoal rubbings taken from an ancient crossroads obelisk reveal fresh chisel marks reversing the safe-water glyphs. Zahra concludes that someone deliberately steered northern relief columns straight into the quicksand sinks.

title: Oakhaven Harbor Tariff Roll
summary: Act III lore book maintained by Harbor-Master Tavin, found in Oakhaven listing maritime duties and timber quotas.

p: Every keel crossing the Greywash bar pays one-tenth of its cargo in weighed silver or refined whale-oil before the boom-chain is lowered. Since Vesperion's black galleys closed the outer straits, drydock pitch has tripled in price and the Merchant Council has bolted the upper tower gates against refugees from Redmarsh. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Salt-stiffened pages detailing anchorage fees, ironwood tonnage, and emergency surcharges levied on every vessel entering the cove. Tavin's neat columns show ordinary merchant trade collapsing overnight into frantic evacuation logistics.

title: Articles of the Bailey Truce
summary: Act III lore book drafted by Guild Speaker Corvus, recovered in Pledge at Oakhaven outlining the frontier pact.

p: Witnessed beneath the petrified oak standards: the Oakhaven Merchant Council hereby opens its subterranean armories and grants forty casks of whale-oil to the northern vanguard, provided mercenaries clear the sunken sea-gates and break Vesperion's blockade before the autumn equinoctial gales trap our fishing fleet inside the bay. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Signed in haste by rival ship-captains and bailiffs who hated each other only slightly less than they feared the inland raiders. The articles trade harbor sanctuary for sworn steel along the northern timber road.

title: Clearance Fire Order
summary: Act III lore book signed by Warden Lyra, found in Cinder Wards ordering the clearance of unstable coastal altars.

p: To deny besiegers timber cover within bowshot of the curtain wall, all tenements between the Tanner's Gate and the old rope-walk shall be cleared and burned at sunset. Citizens failing to remove their belongings before the third horn forfeit compensation. Watch patrols will shoot any looter caught rummaging in the cooling cellars. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

A blunt eviction notice commanding squatters and hedge-cultists off the sulfurous flats before the fractured ward-rings blow. Lyra notes with grim humor that nobody listens to a parchment warning until the ground starts glowing.

title: Moorland Artillery Report
summary: Act III lore book filed by Captain Hale, discovered in Sundered Ranks assessing moorland artillery engagements.

p: Our shield-wall held through two infantry charges until Vesperion's fire-pots arced over the heather ridge and shattered the center ranks. Burning whale-oil ran beneath our greaves, forcing veterans to break formation or roast inside their mail. Twenty-four shields still lie locked edge-to-edge where the third company stood its ground. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Hale's plain-spoken report counts broken carriage wheels, spent powder kegs, and the exact ridge-angles where renegade legions dug in. He advises any future commander to crack both flanks before touching the central crag.

title: Chapel Nave Surgical Log
summary: Act III lore book kept by Surgeon Meris, found in Field Infirmary logging battlefield wounds and bandage shortages.

p: Ran out of clean linen bandages at midnight; tearing altar cloths into strips and boiling them in vinegar brine. Seventeen men need iron shrapnel extracted before gangrene sets in, while enemy scouts probe the churchyard wall every hour. If the picket line breaks, bar the vestry doors and keep the bone-saws within reach. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Spotted with dried blood and vinegar stains, Meris's surgical roll sorts incoming borderers into those who can walk, those who need a saw, and those who only need quiet. The ink grows shakier as the raider packs close in.

title: Citadel Tide & Flood Table
summary: Act III lore book compiled by Keeper Orin, recovered in Sunken Citadel charting flood intervals at the sea-gate.

p: High spring tide floods the lower barbican to a depth of fourteen feet within twenty minutes of the first swell. Heavy infantry caught in the kelp-slick galleries must unbuckle breastplates or drown before the ebb. Only the spiral lighthouse stair above the third sea-arch stays dry when Atlantic gales drive waves against the chalk cliffs. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Carefully calculated high-water marks etched onto waterproofed vellum. Orin warns that anyone caught inside the lower sea-caves when the Western Sea surges will find the iron grates submerged in less than twenty minutes.

title: Shingle Spit Crossing Rules
summary: Act III lore book written by Pilot Bram, found in Hourglass Rescue detailing safe crossing times on the shingle bar.

p: Never start across the Hourglass Spit once the white breakers cover the black anchor-rock at the harbor mouth. The current sweeps sideways across the gravel bar fast enough to knock a laden pack-horse off its legs, and the sea-caves along the cliff face flood completely to their roofs. Count every wave before stepping onto wet gravel. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Bram's salty, no-nonsense rules for running the narrow gravel spit before the tide cuts off the tidal vaults. He adds a dry postscript: if you hear the surf ringing against the iron bars, drop your pack and run.

title: Cliff-Watch Siege Rationing
summary: Act III lore book maintained by Castellan Vane, uncovered in Starved Bastion recording weeks of siege rationing.

p: Day forty-two of the naval blockade. We slaughtered the last baggage mule on Tuesday and melted the chapel's pewter candlesticks into sling-bullets yesterday morning. Vesperion's galleys circle below the cliffs flashing truce lanterns, yet every man on the battlements knows what happened to the prisoners taken at Harborwatch. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Day by day, the daily allowance shrinks from half a loaf to boiled oats, and finally to leather straps softened in rainwater. Yet Vane's handwriting stays steady, vowing the cliff-watch will hold until grain wagons reach the bridge.

title: Canal Floodgate Operating Writ
summary: Act III lore book authored by Lock-Master Durn, found in Riverlock Crossing explaining the canal floodgate gears.

p: To equalize water levels between the Greywash canal and the sea-basin, two teams of four men must turn the bronze capstans in unison while the iron pawls engage every third tooth. If either counterweight chain snaps under full tidal head, the surge will tear the wooden catwalks away and flood three leagues of coastal farmland. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Detailed diagrams of greased iron counterweights, sluice-pins, and freshwater channels feeding Harborwatch's cisterns. Durn warns that opening both gates simultaneously will sweep armored men straight off the stone walkways.

title: Age of Chains Rune-Tablet
summary: Act III lore book inscribed by Arch-Artificer Sol, recovered in Elder Juggernaut detailing ancient titan bindings.

p: Carved into lead-lined slate: 'By the seven iron links of the First Empire, this bedrock frame is bound to guard the coastal pass without sleep, wage, or mercy. Should stray ley-currents ever wake its furnace core, strike the glowing rune-seams between its shoulder plates with cold arcane fire.' The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Translated from cracked Age of Chains stone tablets, Sol's treatise describes how primeval granite colossi were shackled to highland cairns. He warns ominously that deep tectonic tremors can snap every binding rune at once.

title: Sea-Cliff Culverin Orders
summary: Act III lore book issued by Master Gunner Tor, found in High-Stakes Gambit outlining sea-cliff culverin firing arcs.

p: Keep damp wool blankets over the powder casks and never bring an open lantern within ten paces of the loading ramp. Elevated at twelve degrees, our bronze culverins can drop solid iron shot straight through the deck of any galley entering the bay—provided we hold the narrow cliff trail behind us against marine boarders. Two misfires will crack the bronze trunnions. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Smudged with black powder and tallow, Tor's orders list elevation wedges and iron shot allotments for guarding the coastal pass. He grumbles that noble speculators care more about guarding their vaults than feeding his gun crews.

title: Ironclad & Ashen Writ
summary: Act III lore book written by Paymaster Krell, discovered in Clashing Banners detailing the feud between rival warbands.

p: Both the Ironclad Banner and the Ashen Company claim exclusive salvage rights over the coastal plain under conflicting charters signed by Oakhaven's Guild Council. Neither captain will yield a yard of turf until weighed silver is counted onto a drumhead, and both hosts have already deployed pikemen along the storm-swept ridge. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

An exasperated legal summary of how the Ironclad Banner and the Ashen Company went from sharing a camp to slaughtering each other over disputed phosphor-tar casks. Krell concludes that neither side deserves a single copper.

title: Final Lighthouse Entry
summary: Act III lore book penned by Keeper Aldous, found in Burning Harbor recording the final night of the evacuation.

p: Midnight: six black fire-hulks drifted past the outer mole under muffled oars and rammed the anchored grain-sloops. Whale-oil casks burst across the timber quays like liquid sun; the heat has already cracked the lighthouse prism-glass. I am locking the bronze spiral door and throwing the key into the boiling surf. The prism-room fills fast with choking black oil-smoke. Damp soot blurs the final line.

The last pages smell faintly of woodsmoke and sea-salt. Aldous logs the departure of every overloaded caravel slipping past the iron boom-chain, trimming his wick one final time while ash falls thick across the lantern glass.

title: Baron Vane's Smuggling Ledger
summary: Act III lore book kept by Clerk Tibalt, uncovered in Baron Vane's Catacomb Lift listing contraband and bullion.

p: Lowered via the manor counterweight hoist into the sea-caves at low tide: forty ingots of unstamped Deep Quarry iron, twelve crates of Conclave copper wire, and three chests of silver coin paid by Vesperion's agents to leave Harborwatch's sea-gate unbarred during the night raid. The hoist chains are greased with mutton fat. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Double-columned accounts hidden behind a false wine-rack, proving Baron Vane skimmed timber, grain, and silver from the evacuation effort for months. Tibalt's tiny footnote dryly hopes the Baron sinks before his ledger surfaces.

title: Cider-Orchard Blight Report
summary: Herbalist Maren's Act III field report from the Cider Orchard, documenting how coastal blight twisted the fruit trees.

p: The apple trees terraced below the chalk watchtower stopped bearing fruit three autumns after the Ashen Coven buried hanged deserters among their roots. Now their black bark sweats thick violet sap, and hollow skulls hang from the upper branches, whispering names whenever coastal fog rolls inland. Even crows refuse to nest in the upper boughs. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Pressed between the stained pages are blackened apple blossoms that still crumble like soot when touched. Maren traces the rot from the lower irrigation ditches up into the terraces, noting with grim precision the exact week the roots first pulled free of the soil.

title: Ironcamp Smelting Ordinances
summary: Smelting ordinances written by Forgemaster Vok in Act IV Ironcamp, detailing heat quotas and foundry discipline.

p: No apprentice approaches the floor-fissures without wet leather aprons and smoked-quartz goggles. Meteoric star-iron must be drawn at white heat and quenched within four heartbeats in sulfur-rich caldera brine; hesitate a moment longer and the blade turns brittle as cold slag. Waste no meteoric filings on untested apprentices. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Nailed to the main bellows-post with iron spikes because ordinary paste peeled off in the smelter heat. Vok lists the penalties for quenching star-iron in dirty water, leaving slag troughs unskimmed, or arguing with a senior smith while holding tongs.

title: Basalt Highway Mile-Log
summary: Outrider Captain Bren's Act IV mile-log from Heartland March, charting ash drifts and ambushes along the basalt highway.

p: Every milestone along the imperial highway has had its royal crest chiseled out and replaced with the scorched wheel of the Ember Court. Heat rises through our boot-soles from cracks in the basalt paving, and fine grey ash falls steadily even under a cloudless sky. Water-skins run dry twice as fast on the black stone. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Crisp, dusty entries scribbled in the saddle whenever the horses stopped to clear volcanic grit from their nostrils. Bren marks every broken culvert, sulfur fissure, and burned waystation between Highcrest and the northern ridge with soldierly thrift.

title: Shattered Beacon Confession
summary: Watchman Galt's Act IV testimony found in Shattered Beacons, explaining how the highland signal grid was compromised.

p: We took fifty gold sovereigns from Malrik's riders to douse the signal pyres with wet sand and smash the bronze mirrors before the relief column crested the ridge. By the time we realized the Ember vanguard meant to slaughter the garrison too, the iron trapdoor was already barred from the outside. The smoke never rose above the ridge. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Written on the back of a ration chit with a blunt charcoal stub while Galt waited for a relief patrol that never came. He admits taking silver to tilt the focusing mirrors off-axis, swearing he was told it would only blind merchant spies.

title: Outer Curtain Damage Log
summary: Engineer Haldor's Act IV structural log from Besieged Wall, recording masonry fractures along the outer curtain.

p: Seventeen molten slag-stones struck the eastern curtain wall since dawn, cracking three basalt courses and igniting the timber hoardings. Sappers can be heard hammering directly beneath Tower Four. We are rolling barrels of quenching brine onto the parapet to cool the stone before the mortar fails. Two masons fell when the east parapet cracked. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Column after column of mortar weights, cracked merlons, and timber bracing tallies kept through three days of ceaseless bombardment. Haldor's neat margin notes dryly observe that pumice stone absorbs impact well right up until the moment it turns to powder.

title: Malrik's Margin Notes
summary: Annotated Act IV syllabus by Arch-Mage Malrik found in Flight of Malrik, outlining forbidden caldera channeling.

p: The northern towers grow colder every winter because the Anchor Seals bleed Thornvael's natural warmth back into the abyss. With the stolen cipher-keys and two obsidian focusing prisms, we can crack the seventh valve open and flood the upper provinces with eternal summer—regardless of what Ashkarath's wardens claim. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Every printed Collegium theorem is slashed through with furious violet ink and replaced by blunt, ruthless corrections. Reading the margins feels like listening to a brilliant man lose his patience with caution one page at a time.

title: Twin-Gate Assault Orders
summary: Marshal Corin's Act IV assault orders from Twofold Assault, mapping synchronized strikes against the twin chasm gates.

p: Both battering columns must strike the east and west barbicans at the exact third horn-blast so the garrison cannot shift its heavy ballistae between towers. Once the iron-shod oak gates splinter, push pikemen straight into the central bailey and cut the winch-chains before defenders drop the inner portcullis. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Creased along the folds and smudged with oil from a field-lantern, these orders leave no room for hesitation on the suspension bridges. Corin warns his officers that taking one crag without pinning the other merely turns the crossing into a shooting gallery.

title: Trench-Maze Defenses
summary: Ember Tactician Vael's Act IV fortification sketch from Gauntlet of Iron, detailing kill-zones and pitch trenches.

p: Every traverse in the Gauntlet of Iron is angled at sixty degrees so repeating ballistae can sweep the full length of each ditch without exposing their crews. Keep oil-soaked faggots stacked behind the timber revetments; once an assault squad enters the third bend, ignite the pitch and seal the rear gate. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Drawn with cold geometric relish on heavy waxed vellum that shrugs off soot and rain alike. Vael angles every parapet and mortar pit so advancing vanguard troops have nowhere to kneel without catching crossfire from the cliffs.

title: Glacis Watch Standing Orders
summary: Centurion Draven's Act IV standing orders recovered at Outer Rampart, governing watch rotations along the basalt glacis.

p: Volcanic basalt absorbs midday sun until bare hands blister on the merlons, then turns ice-cold within an hour of sunset. Pour boiling slag-oil only when attackers reach the base of the sloped glacis; wasting casks at long range merely coats the stone for their sappers to grip. Keep sand buckets beside every brazier. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Blunt garrison rules written for men who sleep in their armor and eat cold hardbread under falling cinders. Draven forbids lighting cooking fires on the wall, reminding his sentries that the caldera glow already gives snipers plenty to aim at.

title: Star-Fortress Siege Log
summary: Commander Thorne's Act IV siege log from Three-Roads Siege, tracking supply shortages and converging enemy columns.

p: Dust plumes rise simultaneously along the northern, western, and southern causeways. Three separate relief hosts are marching to break our blockade before we can breach the magma moat. Hold the star-bastions at all costs; if any one road opens, the Infernal Citadel will be reinforced before nightfall. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Short, clipped dispatches stamped at hourly intervals as dust clouds rise along all three highland approaches at once. Thorne counts powder kegs, horseshoes, and unbroken halberds with the calm of an officer who intends to sell every yard dearly.

title: Inscription of Headless Kings
summary: Chronicler Zahra's Act IV epigraphic study from Threshold Choice, translating weathered carvings of ancient monarchs.

p: Carved into the obsidian plinths flanking the crossroads: 'Here stood the seven sovereigns who wore the Crown of Order and refused to unbind the Anchor Seals. Their heads were struck off by their own heirs when winter famine gripped the capital, yet their headless stone still guards the fork.' The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Charcoal rubbings reveal rows of sculpted rulers whose crowns were chiseled clean off their brows centuries before the current war. Zahra notes that whoever defaced the stonework did not act in rage—they worked with neat, patient mason's tools.

title: Colonnade Conquest Roll
summary: Imperial Herald Vex's Act IV ledger found in Crown of Order, enumerating ancient campaigns and tribute decrees.

p: Around the black marble pillars hang the tarnished crowns of twelve conquered border provinces, each chained beneath a brazier of never-dying coal. Beneath the seventh pillar lies an empty iron hook stamped with the crest of Thornwick—forged three centuries ago and waiting patiently for its tribute. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Inscribed in stiff ceremonial script that treats conquered provinces like entries in a grain inventory. Vex records exact bushels, iron ingots, and sworn oaths collected from border towns whose names no longer appear on any living map.

title: First Warden's Final Writ
summary: First Warden Ashkarath's Act IV writ from Ember Reckoning, setting down the harsh philosophy of the furnace wardens.

p: Let him who steps onto the Obsidian Dais understand the price of the Primordial Ember: the flame will mend every shattered wardstone and banish winter from Thornvael forever, yet it will burn away every name, face, and oath you ever loved until only iron will remains. The margins are stained with damp soot and river silt. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Cut into thin sheets of dark bronze because ordinary parchment curls to ash inside the lower galleries. The testament reads less like a prayer and more like an ironfounder's manual, weighing mortal endurance against the heat required to purify it.

title: Magnetic Narrows Survey
summary: Sapper Captain Orin's Act IV field survey from Magnetic Canyon, warning troops about lodestone veins pulling iron gear.

p: Do not enter the thirty-pace defile wearing unstrapped plate or loose iron scabbards. The raw lodestone cliffs pull steel blades sideways out of hand and jam crossbow triggers mid-draw. Equip ash-wood staves, horn bows, and boiled leather before advancing beneath the portcullis. Even belt-buckles tug northward inside the gorge. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Orin advises every soldier entering the narrows to strap down loose daggers, leave spare horseshoes behind, and keep compasses in their pockets. Two mules reportedly bolted after their bit-chains snapped straight onto a cliff face.

title: Focusing Crag Readings
summary: Adept Solis's Act IV optical readings from West Beacon Crag, charting refraction angles across the smoky plateau.

p: Whenever the violet capacitor prism on West Crag chimes at high pitch, blue static jumps six paces between grounded copper rods. Malrik's defectors aligned its facets directly toward the Threshold Nave to overload the silver door's containment wards from outside. Grounding wires glow dull red during every discharge. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Dense tables of crystal alignment, midday glare, and copper-wire drift recorded during the final calm month before the grid broke. Solis complains repeatedly that highland winds rattle the mirror frames faster than apprentices can shim them.

title: Seventh Anchor Valve Rubbing
summary: Act IV architectural rubbing by Chronicler Zahra from the Threshold Nave, documenting the seventh anchor valve.

p: Copied from the meteoric-iron valve sunk beside the Threshold Nave: 'Seven seals bleed the mountain's wrath into the deep sea. Break one, and rivers boil; break three, and ash blots out the sun; break all seven, and the Crown of Order becomes a collar of living fire.' Faint heat still rises through the valve's bronze rim. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line. Damp soot blurs the final line.

Fine charcoal dust picks out interlocking rings of First-Dynasty script that match neither imperial law nor Collegium wardcraft. Zahra's hurried postscript observes that the valve housing was built to be turned from the inside, never sealed forever.

title: The First Compact
summary: Act I lore codex unlocked at the Sunken Ford boundary stone, introducing the founding treaty of the northern border.
infobox: Inspect the boundary stone at Sunken Ford.

p: Signed in iron and tallow between border lords and exiled dwarven smith-clans, the Compact bound each province to maintain the mountain drainage galleries (see cdx-undervault-galleries) and weather-wards. Three centuries of tax-skimming reduced the treaty to rotted vellum.

Long before salt-tithe bailiffs rode north with iron shackles, three frontier barons met beside the Alder shallows to carve a plain promise into granite. The stone still stands half-buried in nettles, though few living clerks bother to read its terms.

title: The Salt Tithe
summary: Act I lore codex unlocked via a Border Mint tax writ, detailing the Crown's punishing wartime extraction levy.
infobox: Find a Border Mint tax writ in Act I.

p: An emergency wartime levy drafted by High Quartermaster Morvessa (see cdx-morvessa-ledger) to strip northern border parishes of brine, grain, and iron ore. Clerks weighed salt on apothecary scales while watchmen starved on promissory slips.

Sold to the northern parishes as a temporary emergency measure to shore up southern walls, the Salt Tithe quickly stripped barns, smithies, and strongboxes clean. Quartermasters weigh silver, iron, and grain on the same merciless scale.

title: The Climate Wardstones
summary: Act II lore codex unlocked by inspecting a ruptured obelisk, explaining the quartz spires that steady Redmarsh.
infobox: Examine a ruptured wardstone in m16.

p: Twelve primeval quartz monoliths driven into the Redmarsh plateau (see cdx-plateau-spires) to anchor rain-clouds and pin alkali dust below the highland passes. When blood-chanters cracked three spires, hot grit drifted north within hours.

Built across the high plateau to break alkali storms and keep caravan roads passable, the three quartz monoliths hummed quietly for generations. Without steady copper grounding and clean runes, the desert reclaims its wind in a single afternoon.

title: Third-Dynasty Probate Law
summary: Act II lore codex unlocked from a Redmarsh funerary tablet, outlining ancient probate law that outlasts death.
infobox: Recover a funerary tablet in Redmarsh.

p: Before the inland sea evaporated into Redmarsh, coastal magistrates ruled that unpaid tax liens survive death. Crypt Embalmers (see cdx-crypt-embalmers) still enforce those decrees with bitumen jars and bone hooks.

Third-Dynasty magistrates considered dying an unconvincing excuse to default on silver owed to the treasury. Under their statutes, copper wire and stamped bitumen tablets kept a debtor's service active inside the salt vaults long after his funeral.

title: The Age of Chains
summary: Act III lore codex unlocked after felling an Elder Juggernaut, recounting the ancient era of bound stone titans.
infobox: Defeat an Elder Juggernaut in Act III.

p: An era of geo-sorcery when border kings bound living bedrock into Elder Juggernauts (see cdx-elder-juggernauts) to patrol mountain passes without wages or rations. Most rusted into scree; a few still wake when ley-currents surge.

Old highland ballads speak of artificers who shackled living rock to mountain cairns with iron-runed collars to guard passes without paying wages. Centuries of quiet rain rusted the chains, leaving the mountains full of irritable sleepers.

title: The Whale-Oil Charter
summary: Act III lore codex unlocked at a burned Harborwatch pier, tracing how coastal charters controlled frontier lantern oil.
infobox: Inspect a burned pier in Harborwatch.

p: Oakhaven's merchant guild grew rich refining lamp oil for Harborwatch's great lighthouse (see cdx-harborwatch-mole). When war closed the straits, privateers hoarded the casks as naval incendiaries.

Every fog-lantern from Fenwick Peat to Oakhaven's lighthouses depended on casks boiled down along the Western Sea. When guild factors hoarded the oil to drive up winter prices, inland crossings went dark one road-post at a time.

title: The Anchor Seals
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by reading an Anchor Seal inscription, explaining the ancient locks holding the caldera.
infobox: Read an Anchor Seal inscription in Act IV.

p: Seven meteoric-iron valves sunk into the caldera floor to bleed primordial magma pressure away from the upper provinces. First Warden Ashkarath (see cdx-ashkarath-watch) starved the realm of warmth rather than risk unbinding them.

Massive rings of star-iron and pale stone buried beneath the basalt peaks to bleed tectonic pressure harmlessly into the crust. Modern scholars can copy the outer markings, yet nobody alive remembers how to forge a replacement valve.

title: The Crown of Order
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked at the Threshold silver door, examining the austere First-Dynasty doctrine of immutable law.

p: Forged from fallen star-iron and quenched in alpine snow, the diadem was meant to bind sovereigns to the soil's health. Chronicler Zahra's rubbings suggest it began as a collar of servitude.

Carved into pale marble where dust never seems to settle, the doctrine argues that chaos is the sole author of human misery. Its keepers prized stillness above comfort, willing to freeze an entire realm rather than watch it fracture.

title: The Primordial Ember
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked near the molten seal in the Threshold, detailing the volcanic doctrine of cleansing fire.
infobox: Approach the molten seal in m44.

p: The unquenched furnace beneath the Obsidian Throne (see cdx-obsidian-dais). It offers strength enough to reshape Thornvael's climate, yet burns away every memory not anchored by iron will.

Opposed in every syllable to the cold marble of Order, the Ember treatises view decay as a sickness cured only by white heat. Smelters and fanatics alike quote its lines whenever soft compromises fail under pressure.

title: Arcane Thermodynamics
summary: Act II lore codex unlocked through mages or Zahra, explaining how Collegium scholars measure mana as heat and pressure.
infobox: Speak with a mage hero or Zahra.

p: Expelled Capital Collegium scholars proved that invocation syllables act as pressure valves on ambient ley-currents. Misfires occur not from divine wrath, but from damp chalk and sloppy grounding.

Frontier arcanists have little patience for poetic talk about spirits and starlight; they treat ley-lines like steam pipes that burst when over-pressured. Keep your circuits grounded and your margins wide, or your own staff will cook your knuckles.

title: Mortuary Debt-Rolls
summary: Act I lore codex unlocked by witnessing spirit binding, detailing how parish clerks balance debt-rolls past the grave.
infobox: Witness a spirit binding in combat.

p: Among border abbeys, necromancy is practiced as strict probate bookkeeping: summoning dead debtors to finish unfulfilled oaths before granting final rest.

In the lower parishes, a necromancer rarely wears dramatic black robes—he wears ink-stained sleeves and carries a brass scale. Every raised skeleton is logged by name, shift, and remaining balance until its tally finally clears.

title: The Caldera Schism
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked via Malrik's syllabus cylinders, tracing the bitter ideological split inside the Collegium.

p: When Arch-Mage Malrik (see cdx-malrik-defection) traded his sight to read volcanic veins, half the Crown College followed him south, preferring eternal ash to growing cold in northern towers.

What began as a dry faculty dispute over caldera survey numbers ended in burned libraries, expelled fellows, and stolen cipher-keys. Half the scholars fled toward the coastal fleet; the rest marched inland to study the fire up close.

title: Thornwick Market
summary: Act I place codex unlocked upon entering Thornwick Market, profiling the palisaded river hub of the northern front.
infobox: Enter Thornwick Market in Act I.

p: A mud-walled river town straddling three peat roads and a timber toll-bridge (see cdx-alder-span). Its plank palisades bristle with sharpened stakes while merchants weigh grain behind shuttered stalls.

Tucked inside a muddy bend of the Alder River, Thornwick was built to trade timber, eels, and salt-pork rather than anchor a war. Between the ringing smithy, the crowded tavern, and the bailiff's hall, it remains the last dry roof for leagues.

title: Alder Bridge
summary: Act I place codex unlocked by defending Alder Bridge, describing the three-arched stone crossing over the border river.

p: Three-century-old oak-and-stone crossing spanning the swollen Alder River. Sole artery wide enough for wheeled artillery between Thornwick and the high moors.

Constructed from dressed grey granite anchored to twin ancient ley-piers, Alder Bridge is the only road capable of carrying heavy grain wagons south. Hold its arches and the northern parishes breathe; lose them and the river turns into a trap.

title: The Undervault Links
summary: Act I place codex unlocked upon descending into the Undervault, detailing the old dwarven drainage tunnels.
infobox: Descend into the Undervault in m10.

p: Three miles of ventilated dwarven stone tunnels cut beneath the northern granite ridge during the First Compact (see cdx-first-compact). Damp mortar and lead-sealed armories line its dark galleries.

Cut cleanly beneath the southern ridges to keep spring meltwater from washing out the border highway. Centuries of neglect left the lead grates clogged with silt, turning dry service corridors into damp ambush alleys.

title: Ashbrook Gatehouse
summary: Act I place codex unlocked after surviving Ashbrook, profiling the fortified southern gatehouse facing the wastes.

p: Southern hinge of the Border Fords frontier, reduced to smoldering timber and turnip-field graves when Velen's rams broke the outer bars.

Once a proud toll-manor inspecting caravans bound for the wet northern pastures, Ashbrook's iron doors mark the sharp line where grass yields to red clay. Sentries stationed on its wall always keep wet rags handy for southern dust.

title: Redmarsh Stockade
summary: Act II place codex unlocked on arriving at Redmarsh Stockade, describing the stilted desert hub above alkali flats.
infobox: Arrive at Redmarsh Outpost in Act II.

p: A sinking timber-and-earth fort braced on oak pilings above rust-red alkali silt. Water sells by the gill while leeches fatten in the stagnant moat.

Hoisted thirty feet clear of the boot-eating brine on limestone pilings and lashed to bleached leviathan ribs. Everything in Redmarsh creaks in the dry wind, and a polite greeting matters far less than whether you brought clean water.

title: The Quartz Plateau
summary: Act II place codex unlocked upon climbing the Quartz Plateau, profiling the high tableland of climate obelisks.
infobox: Climb the Quartz Plateau in m16.

p: Wind-scoured alkali mesa crowned by primeval climate wardstones (see cdx-wardstone-lattice). Static discharge turns exposed steel blue before desert squalls strike.

Blinding white limestone stretches flat toward the horizon, broken only by three fractured quartz pillars that hum loud enough to ache in the teeth. When the spires fall out of tune, alkali gales strip paint straight off wagon boards.

title: The Deep Quarry
summary: Act II place codex unlocked by liberating the terraces, describing the stepped basalt mine worked by northern debtors.
infobox: Liberate the quarry terraces in m20.

p: A four-hundred-foot terraced pit sunk into a volcanic fault for dense black ironstone. Flooded at the bottom with black rainwater and ringed by rusted slave-cranes.

Three sheer tiers cut deep into black ironstone, echoing day and night with sledgehammers, wooden crane winches, and iron collars. Half the fortifications in the South were built from stone pried out of this dusty pit.

title: Ironheart Bastion
summary: Act II place codex unlocked upon storming Ironheart Bastion, profiling the twin bridges guarding the mountain gates.

p: Black-slag fortress crowning twin volcanic spires above sinking salt-bogs and cannon-swept causeways. Controls the sole mountain pass to the Iron Coast.

Two razor-thin stone causeways span a mile-deep gorge where freezing mist vents from rusted mountain pipes. Imperial engineers designed the approaches so a handful of armored men could hold back an entire starving province.

title: Oakhaven Bastion
summary: Act III place codex unlocked upon entering Oakhaven, describing the cliffside timber port overlooking the Western Sea.

p: Walled hill-city anchored around petrified cedar pilings where the Greywash meets the sea. Slate roofs, guild curfew bells, and drydocks smelling of pine pitch.

Ringed by ancient ironwood groves that built half the Crown's merchant fleet, Oakhaven smells perpetually of pine sap, oakum, and salt spray. Its stone bailiff's gate now serves as the main funnel for inland survivors seeking the coast.

title: The Sunken Citadel
summary: Act III place codex unlocked by breaching the water-gate, profiling the half-submerged fortress carved into sea-caves.

p: First-Empire sea-stack fortress tilted ten cubits into the Atlantic swell. Spring tides flood its lower barbican twice daily, trapping armored men in kelp-slick halls.

Built when the Western Sea sat ten feet lower, this slate stronghold now floods twice daily through corroded iron grates. Barnacle-crusted ramparts and knee-deep courtyards turn every advance into a treacherous race against the tide.

title: Harborwatch Anchorage
summary: Act III place codex unlocked by retaking the seawalls, describing the granite fortress-harbor and war-docks.
infobox: Retake the seawall batteries in m35.

p: Deep-water port guarded by bronze sea-wall culverins and a whale-oil lighthouse visible for forty leagues. Torched during Admiral Kael's blockade.

Massive breakwaters, heavy iron boom-chains, and swinging timber cranes project straight into the gray swells. Harborwatch is the last working anchorage on the Iron Coast, holding open the sea-lanes while inland roads burn.

title: The Obsidian Dais
summary: Act IV place codex unlocked upon reaching the Threshold Chamber, profiling the ancient subterranean hall of choice.
infobox: Reach the Threshold Chamber in m44.

p: Geometric basalt sanctuary at the exact center of the volcanic caldera, split by magma moats and crowned by the glass throne of the First Emperors.

Deep beneath the caldera's outer ramparts, volcanic roar fades into an oppressive, echoing hush. Twin platforms of pale marble and glowing basalt face each other across the flagstones, waiting without haste for a mortal verdict.

title: Thornwick Border Levy
summary: Act I faction codex unlocked via Sergeant Garrick, detailing the stubborn border militia holding the northern roads.

p: Underpaid provincial pikemen and bridge-wardens commanded by Sergeant Garrick (see cdx-garrick-watch). Stubborn in mud trenches, chronically short of crossbow bolts and dry boots.

Farmers, sawyers, and river-ferrymen handed pitted pikes and told to look fierce whenever raiders cross the fords. They grumble about late wages and wet boots, yet when their own roofs are at stake, few regulars stand firmer.

title: The Salt-Tithe Commission
summary: Act I faction codex unlocked after clashing with bailiffs, profiling the Crown's ruthless fiscal extraction corps.
infobox: Clashes with bailiffs in Act I.

p: Armed tax-bailiffs, ledger-clerks, and arson-companies organized by Morvessa to foreclose on border granaries and iron mines.

Backed by stamped writs and hired steel, the commission's clerks arrive with brass scales and leave with everything that is not bolted to bedrock. They insist their ledgers are merely arithmetic, never personal cruelty.

title: The Ashen Coven
summary: Act I faction codex unlocked at Mordred's altar, describing the shadowy cultists drawn to border ruins and pyres.

p: Renegade hedge-mages and blood-chanters led by Mordred and Hexer Saelen who tap subterranean ley-fissures to rot crops and animate drowned corpses.
