A loose rabble of disgraced chanters and hedge-necromancers who see the creeping southern warmth as a divine invitation. They nest in flooded crypts and burned kilns, trading dark favors for ash-stained relics.

title: Redmarsh Sand-Clans
summary: Act II faction codex unlocked after repelling a canyon ambush, detailing the nomadic raiders of the Redmarsh passes.
infobox: Repel a canyon ambush in Act II.

p: Nomadic dune-raiders riding wind-scoured arroyos with horn-bows and curved scimitars. Armed with contraband Deep Quarry iron to bleed northern supply trains.

Lean, sun-baked skirmishers who know every blind gully and dry waterhole between the Ochre Ditch and the mountains. They care nothing for northern rights or southern crowns, selling their hornbows to whoever pays in coin and clean water.

title: Oakhaven Merchant Council
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked when negotiating coastal entry, profiling the shrewd merchant council ruling Oakhaven.

p: Wealthy timber-barons and tower-adepts who tax both smugglers and royal galleys, hoarding salt-beef behind bolted gates until the blockade threatens their drydocks.

Timber barons, ship-factors, and tariff clerks who spent decades squabbling over berth fees and whale-oil quotas. Faced with a burning continent, they still insist on counting every barrel of flour before opening the gate.

title: The Ironclad Banner
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked in Clashing Banners, describing the heavy mercenary legion fighting for coastal spoils.

p: A mercenary host of coastal pike-men stitched under rust-dyed sailcloth. Loyal strictly to weighed silver and quick to turn on employers who pay in clipped tin.

Disciplined ex-regulars clad in uniform grey plate who turned freelance the day imperial pay-chests stopped arriving. They march in tight shield-walls and treat salvage rights as the only law left standing.

title: The Ashen Company
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked by breaking rival warbands, profiling the zealous free-company warring against the Ironclads.
infobox: Break the rival banners in m34.

p: Rival sellswords recruited from burned fishing towns along the Iron Coast, locked in bloody turf wars with the Ironclad Banner over harbor salvage.

Painted with sulfur stripes and armed with phosphor-tar pots, these reckless raiders despise formal charters and merchant councils alike. Where the Ashen Banner camps, timber yards usually end the night as charcoal.

title: Vesperion's Black Fleet
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked after fighting marine boarders, detailing Vesperion's hostile fleet patrolling the coast.
infobox: Fight marine boarders in Act III.

p: Copper-sheeted war galleys and fire-hulks commanded by Lord Admiral Vesperion to burn coastal shipyards and prevent armies from crossing to the caldera.

Tar-hulled galleys flying no national flag, crewed by hard-bitten press-gang sailors and sea-hardened arcanists. They prowl the outer fogbanks beyond the boom-chain, preying on overloaded transports and coastal lighthouses.

title: Ironcamp Forge-Guild
summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked at Vok's forge, profiling the stubborn master smiths working beside volcanic vents.

p: Keloid-scarred smiths and siege-sappers led by Forgemaster Vok who quench meteoric steel in open caldera fissures.

Deafened by trip-hammers and scarred by flying sparks, the forge-guild stayed behind on the basalt ridge because nowhere else burns hot enough to smelt meteoric iron. They judge every soldier solely by how well he maintains his edge.

title: The Scorched Penitents
summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked via Brother Elias, describing the ash-marked zealots enduring the caldera approaches.

p: Blind battle-mages and ash-robed archivists following Brother Elias, bearing iron collars to atone for opening the caldera's first cinder-gates.

Former abbey clerks and scarred survivors who marched inland carrying iron censers and heavy chains to atone for the realm's sins. Unsettling to share a campfire with, yet strangely calm when lava rains from the sky.

title: The First Watch
summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked by finding ancient plate, detailing the forgotten pre-schism order of the Threshold.
infobox: Find a First Watch plate in Act IV.

p: Ancient wardens who sealed the volcanic threshold centuries ago. Many remain bound to obsidian pillars as unquiet witnesses awaiting formal discharge.

Long before modern barons argued over tolls, the First Watch stood silent guard over the continent's deep tectonic locks. Only cracked armor, blank signets, and stern stone inscriptions remain to mark their centuries of vigil.

title: Dread Vanguard of the Throne
summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked upon facing a Dread Knight, profiling the heavy armored shock troops of the Iron Pact.
infobox: Face a Dread Knight in Act IV.

p: Meteor-plated champions and magma-forged constructs guarding the Gauntlet of Iron and the Anchor Seals under First Warden Ashkarath.

Sealed inside blackened steel tempered over slag channels, these elite fanatics march without banners, music, or mercy. They view ordinary mortal armies as soft ore waiting to be hammered clean in the caldera's heat.

title: Briar Hound
summary: Act I creature codex unlocked at Sunken Ford, examining the thorn-matted pack rushers of the northern thickets.
infobox: Slay Briar Hounds at the Sunken Ford.

p: Feral border curs colonized by parasitic iron-bramble growing directly through their ribs. Hunt in starving packs along river shallows; vulnerable to fire.

Border woodsmen blame wet winters and unburied war-dead for turning ordinary stray dogs into gaunt, vicious curs. Tangled blackthorn twigs mat their coats into natural bramble-armor that tears at bare calves.

title: Flintback
summary: Act I creature codex unlocked in the northern woods, studying the slow, chert-plated beasts blocking timber roads.
infobox: Encounter a Flintback in Act I.

p: Quarry-beasts whose dorsal hides calcified into overlapping slabs of grey chert. Arrows glance off; crack their posture with heavy mauls or lightning.

Broad, bad-tempered grazers whose dorsal scales calcify into grey flint hard enough to turn a woodcutter's hatchet. Wise hunters leave them to chew roots in peace unless a mage is handy to crack their backs.

title: Mire Wisp
summary: Act I creature codex unlocked after a fen ambush, explaining the pale marsh-gas casters haunting bog boardwalks.
infobox: Survive a fen ambush in m02.

p: Pockets of marsh methane and spiteful lingering memory anchored inside drowned livestock skulls. Disperse them with fire before corpse-gas chokes the vanguard.

Peat-cutters tell rookies never to trust a steady blue flame floating off the timber planks after dusk. Mire wisps mimic lantern-light to lure patrols into waist-deep muck before pelting them with freezing bolts.

title: Dune Lurker
summary: Act II creature codex unlocked in Bracken Basin, profiling the sand-burrowing ambushers of the Redmarsh wastes.
infobox: Cross Bracken Basin in Act II.

p: Ochre-shelled desert mantids buried up to their eyes in dry creek beds. Erupt behind stragglers with serrated scythe-limbs; chill them with frost.

Flat-backed predators that shimmy beneath warm red grit until only a faint ripple betrays their hiding place. Caravan guards keep iron-shod prods moving ahead of the mules to force lurkers out before they strike.

title: Basalt Brute
summary: Act II creature codex unlocked upon facing one in the wastes, examining the animated quarry giants of the frontier.
infobox: Face a Basalt Brute in Act II.

p: Walking siege-engines of hexagonal black rock animated by caldera pressure. Immobilize their wide feet with ice magic and chip them down from range.

Quarried from dense volcanic rock and bound with crude siege-runes to serve as tireless shock troops. Arrows splinter uselessly off their chests, leaving only lightning and arcane fire to split their heavy mineral seams.

title: Crypt Embalmer
summary: Act II creature codex unlocked in the lower quarry gallery, studying the ancient linen-wrapped mages of the salt vaults.
infobox: Enter the lower quarry gallery in m20.

p: Third-Dynasty mortuary priests whose hollowed ribs house venomous copperheads. Burn them from afar before their bitumen fumes rot wounds.

Preserved in dry bitumen and copper wire, Third-Dynasty embalmers still patrol their sunken archives with grim persistence. Left unchecked behind enemy lines, they stitch fallen raiders back upright faster than swords can drop them.

title: Salt Crab
summary: Act III creature codex unlocked on the low-tide flats, profiling the armored coastal crustaceans blocking beach paths.
infobox: Wade the low-tide flats in m28.

p: Tidal crustaceans that cement brine-crystals and wrecked hull planks onto their shells. Flank their massive left shield-claw or boil them with lightning.

Heavy-shelled scavengers that clatter out of tide-pools whenever battle spills blood into the brine. Their wet carapaces conduct lightning cleanly, making storm-casters far more effective against them than ordinary swordsmen.

title: Elder Juggernaut
summary: Act III creature codex unlocked after felling the ridge sentinel, studying the colossal bound titans of the highlands.
infobox: Defeat the ridge sentinel in m32.

p: Colossal bedrock constructs bound during the Age of Chains (see cdx-age-of-chains). Conventional steel bounces off; target glowing rune-seams with arcane fire.

Towering frames of anthracite and iron wedges that slept beneath highland cairns for generations until tectonic tremors snapped their tethers. Every footstep splits granite trails and sends boulders tumbling down the passes.

title: Frost Bell
summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by shattering one on the coast, examining the hovering bronze bells of flooded crypts.
infobox: Shatter a Frost Bell in Act III.

p: Levitating liturgical bronze bells torn from drowned chapels. Their skull-clappers ring sub-audible chimes that freeze mana and crack mortar.

Cast from cracked abbey metal and animated by cold astral currents, these silent relics drift through damp halls tolling a freezing note. Bowstrings snap and fingers stiffen within paces of their chime.

title: Night Orchard
summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by clearing the terraced grove, profiling the uprooted, ward-warped cider trees.
infobox: Clear the terraced grove in Act III.

p: Gallows-trees animated by shadow covens, bearing screaming magenta skulls like winter fruit. Chop them down with fire-enchanted axes.

Gnarled coastal fruit trees that drank too much runoff from leaking grave-wards and pulled their knotted roots free of the loam. They stalk dimly lit terraces, snaring patrols in crackling astral brambles.

title: Anvilmaw Smith
summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked by hunting one in the caldera, studying the slag-forged hammer titans.
infobox: Hunt an Anvilmaw in Act IV.

p: Cinderforge siege-titans with iron anvils for lower jaws and smoking chimneys on their spines. Scatter when they raise their hammer-arms toward their chins.

Lumbering horrors born where volcanic vents fused abandoned foundry anvils into living metal. They swing white-hot hammers with terrifying reach, forcing frontline troops to chill their joints and kite between blows.

title: Redglass Drake
summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked by spotting one in the highlands, examining the volcanic glass-scaled fire flyers.
infobox: Spot a Redglass Drake in Act IV.

p: Volcanic ridge dragons with razor-sharp obsidian wing-membranes. Ground them with cold magic and stay clear of their molten glass breath.
Swift winged reptiles whose hides vitrified into jagged crimson glass along the caldera rims. Roosting on basalt chimneys, they dive through cinder-snow to scorch supply trains and melt iron helmets.

title: Massacre at Sunken Ford
summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Blood at the Ford, recounting the gnoll raid that exposed border corruption.

p: Grok'tar's gnoll warband butchered the Thornwick night-watch at dawn, torching the tollhouse to hide forged Border Mint dispatches.

What looked at dawn like another routine raid across the Alder shallows quickly turned sour when dead gnolls spilled fresh southern copper into the mud. The skirmish proved Thornwick's real enemies were not all across the river.

title: The Broken Picket
summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Nightfall at Ravenwatch, recording how the northern keep fell from within.

p: Four watchmen abandoned Ravenwatch's outer wall before nightfall, pulling the iron stakes from inside to lure defenders away from the Sunken Sanctum.

No battering ram ever touched Ravenwatch's iron portcullis; the chains were filed through quietly from the inside before midnight. The breach taught border officers that unpaid debts can break a wall faster than siege engines.

title: The Alder Bridge Stand
summary: Act I event codex unlocked after Alder Bridge, chronicling the desperate stand that saved Thornwick's refugees.

p: Three thousand river-parish refugees crossed Alder Bridge under arrow cover while pikemen held three successive raider waves on the slick oak planks.

Three ragged waves of deserters and brigands crashed against the three-arched stone span while farm carts rumbled south behind the shields. The bridge held by a hair, buying the northern parishes one more breath.

title: The Burning of Ashbrook
summary: Act I event codex unlocked upon completing Act I, recording the fierce fighting that opened the southern road.

p: Unable to hold shattered timber gates against Velen's rams, the vanguard sallied out to slay the commander and escort survivors south into Redmarsh.

Smoke rolled across the northern pastures as the gatehouse garrison fought to keep the heavy iron doors from sealing shut forever. Breaking through Ashbrook marked the moment a local tax war became a continental march.

title: The Wardstone Rupture
summary: Act II event codex unlocked after Wardstone Rupture, detailing the sabotage and cleansing of Redmarsh's spires.

p: Ashen Coven sorcerers cracked three quartz wardstones to test sigil-breaking rituals, unleashing scouring copper dust storms across Bracken Basin.

For weeks an unnatural alkali storm pinned caravans inside their stockades until field scholars uncovered reverse blood-runes chiseled into the monolith bases. Re-grounding the three stones cleared the sky in a single silent flash.

title: The Deep Quarry Revolt
summary: Act II event codex unlocked after Deep Quarry, chronicling the uprising of chained northern debtors in the pits.

p: Chained ironstone miners broke their pens with stolen picks during the vanguard assault, flooding the pit and starving Gorrathul's forges of ore.

When crane counterweights crashed into the overseer barracks and iron collars snapped open across three terraces, the southern army lost its main stone supply overnight. Miners traded picks for pikes and never looked back.

title: The Lie of Ironheart
summary: Act II event codex unlocked upon completing Act II, recording the shattering discovery behind Ironheart's gates.

p: Gorrathul bled two thousand men defending Ironheart's forked cisterns, only for victors to discover the lower aquifers had silted dry years earlier.

Thousands crossed the blistering alkali flats trusting the old mountain reservoirs to save them from the coming heat. Breaking past the frozen sluice-gates revealed a harsher enemy than any army: fifty years of dry red silt.

title: The Oakhaven Truce
summary: Act III event codex unlocked after Pledge at Oakhaven, recounting the tense alliance forged at the timber port.

p: After mercenaries cleared the channel blockade, Oakhaven's council opened its armories and pledged coastal marines for the southern crossing.

Merchant factors and frontier soldiers seldom trust each other, yet the sight of inland raiders burning the pine road concentrated minds wonderfully. Steel bought harbor shelter, and shelter bought time to rig the fleet.

title: The Burning of Harborwatch
summary: Act III event codex unlocked upon completing Act III, chronicling the fiery rearguard defense of the war-docks.

p: Admiral Vesperion torched drydocks and fishing sloops to deny troop transports, losing his flagship when reclaimed seawall guns shattered his rudder.

Ash fell thick as winter sleet across the granite piers while overloaded caravels slipped past the iron boom-chain one by one. Those who held the burning flagstones traded their own passage for the fleet's clean wind.

title: Flight of Arch-Mage Malrik
summary: Act IV event codex unlocked after Flight of Malrik, documenting the pursuit of the Collegium's grand conspirator.

p: Malrik fled Ironcamp with stolen cipher-keys and leyline codices, dying on the summit portal stairs before he could seal the inner sanctum.

Cornered on the switchbacks of Ashveil Gorge with stolen cipher-keys stuffed inside his coat, Malrik proved how far a scholar will run when his arithmetic turns to treason. Recovering his ledgers exposed the Iron Pact's inner design.

title: Battle of Three-Roads Watch
summary: Act IV event codex unlocked after Three-Roads Siege, recording the breaking of the Iron Pact's flanking columns.

p: Three converging relief armies were defeated in detail across the ash plains, isolating the Infernal Citadel behind its magma moats.

Three heavy siege columns converged simultaneously on the highland junction, aiming to starve the vanguard before it reached the inner ramparts. Holding the star-redoubt and counter-marching north shattered their reserve camp completely.

title: The Threshold Reckoning
summary: Act IV event codex unlocked upon completing Act IV, chronicling the decisive confrontation beneath the caldera.

p: At the geometric heart of the caldera, the last Anchor Seals fractured—forcing Thornvael's liberators to choose between pale starlight and living ember.

Beyond the outer walls and the screaming magma channels lies a quiet stone chamber where steel alone cannot settle the account. Whatever verdict is struck upon the Threshold alters every road and harbor across Thornvael.

title: The Reversed Basalt Pillars
summary: Act III place codex unlocked by inspecting slag wedges in Cinder Wards, explaining how coastal pillars were sabotaged.
infobox: Inspect the cracked slag wedges beside the middle ward-ring in Cinder Wards.

p: Carved originally to cool Oakhaven's deep aquifer, these three basalt obelisks were inverted by crimson fire-binders using wedges of meteoric slag. Instead of drawing heat from the rock, they pump subterranean steam straight into the water table until wells boil at noon.

Someone drove rough furnace-slag shims beneath the basalt ward-rings to invert their cooling draft into scorching vents. Field arcanists call it clumsy engineering, though it cleared the flats efficiently enough.

title: Split Tooth Redoubts
summary: Act III place codex unlocked via the western bunker range-slate in Sundered Ranks, detailing moorland redoubts.
infobox: Read the range-slate bolted inside the western arbalest bunker in Sundered Ranks.

p: Named for a sixty-foot splinter of coastal granite cleaved by winter frost, Split Tooth turns a single wagon track into two narrow killing alleys. Imperial engineers built twin stone arbalest bunkers on either shoulder so every square yard of gravel can be swept twice.

Chalked distances and windage marks cover the slate bolted beside the arbalest slit, showing exactly where passing supply columns slow down on the grade. Renegade officers knew the ridge better than the men who built it.

title: Sera's Field-Hospital Roll
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked at the chapel medicine chest in Field Infirmary, profiling Sera's triage company.
infobox: Examine the blood-spotted medicine chest behind the chapel in Field Infirmary.

p: Barber-surgeon Sera keeps two ledgers in her apron: brown ink for men who need stitches, charcoal for men who need a priest. When raiders ringed the chapel bracken, she refused to abandon a single stretcher until the last splinted leg was lashed to the Triage Wagon.

Inside the blood-spotted lid sits a neat list of boiled linen, willow-bark, and laudanum rations stretched across three times too many stretchers. Sera's helpers work without complaint, asking only that the perimeter shields hold.

title: Tide-Clock of the Sunken Citadel
summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the brass tide-gauge in Sunken Citadel, explaining the sea-gate flood clock.
infobox: Check the corroded brass tide-gauge by the water-gate in Sunken Citadel.

p: Built atop a listing sea-stack off Ironcamp coast, the Sunken Citadel relies on a brass tide-wheel wired to its lighthouse bell. At spring flood, seawater pours through kelp-choked sluices and drowns the lower courtyard in less than two glasses.

Green verdigris cakes the dial face, yet the heavy counterweight chain still ticks reliably with the Western Sea's swell. Every veteran who enters the water-gate learns to read the gauge before stepping onto the lower flags.

title: Fourteen Bolts at Iron-Gate
summary: Act III lore codex unlocked via parapet tally marks in Hourglass Rescue, commemorating a desperate tower stand.
infobox: Inspect the tally marks carved into the watchtower parapet in Hourglass Rescue.

p: Gate Warden Lyra rationed her watchtower's last fourteen crossbow quarrels by chalking one name onto each ash shaft. None were wasted on shields; every bolt was saved for an officer's throat or a torch-bearer's oilskin.

Fourteen deep knife-notches scored into wet granite beside a broken crossbow stirrup. Whoever held the watchtower while the tide crept up the shingle spit counted every last bolt before the iron bars went under.

title: High-Orchard Cisterns
summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the dry rain tank in Starved Bastion, detailing the fortress's failed water supply.
infobox: Check the dry lead-lined rain tank inside the courtyard in Starved Bastion.

p: Perched on porous chalk above the coastal orchards, this redoubt can turn aside a month of siege-rams yet holds barely four days of rainwater in its lead-lined tanks. Every garrison commander lives in dread of an ambushed mule-train.

Lead-lined cisterns built to catch coastal squalls stand dusty and cracked after weeks of hot inland wind. Scraping dry rust off the bottom trough explains why the cliff garrison greeted four grain wagons like a miracle.

title: Riverlock Counterweight Gears
summary: Act III place codex unlocked at the central sluice gear-housing in Riverlock Crossing, explaining the canal machinery.
infobox: Examine the greased iron gear-housing on the central sluice island in Riverlock Crossing.

p: Eighty feet above black river rapids, twin stone bridges rest on hollow piers housing eight-ton iron counterweights. A single pulled pin drops the floodgates, turning a dry crossing into a roaring sluice in ten heartbeats.

Heavy cast-iron teeth slick with sheep-tallow drive twin oak floodgates weighing ten tons apiece. Control the central island and you control both freshwater for the harbor docks and the footing of anyone crossing below.

title: Age of Chains Colossus
summary: Act III creature codex unlocked by inspecting an anthracite rib-plate, studying the construction of the Elder Juggernaut.
infobox: Inspect a shattered anthracite rib-plate after felling the Elder Juggernaut.

p: Bound with dwarf-forged links and packed with anthracite, these bedrock walkers were built to haul siege-towers across mountain passes. Centuries of pine moss hide their granite plates until an intruder wakes the furnace roaring inside their ribs.

Up close, the fallen titan's hide is not natural stone at all, but layered volcanic coal fused with ancient copper staples. Artificers of the Age of Chains built their guardians to outlast empires, not merely skirmishes.

title: Baron Vane's Extortion Ledger
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked via the bullion manifest in High-Stakes Gambit, exposing Baron Vane's wartime profiteering.
infobox: Read the stamped bullion manifest inside Vane's eastern vault in High-Stakes Gambit.

p: Turncoat Baron Vane taxed every herring barrel and anchor chain on the Ironcamp coast, melting the silver into unmarked ingots in his manor cellar. His catacomb lift was rigged to drop straight to a smuggler's cove the moment honest steel knocked at his gate.

Stamped bars of northern silver sit neatly stacked beside extortion writs levied on desperate ship-captains. Even with the horizon glowing red, Baron Vane treated the collapse of the realm as a buyer's market.

title: The Salvage Quarrel
summary: Act III faction codex unlocked at the phosphor-tar casks in Clashing Banners, explaining the bloody mercenary feud.
infobox: Inspect the disputed phosphor-tar casks in the muddy hollow in Clashing Banners.

p: The Ironclad Banner and the Ashen Company spent six months looting the same wrecked harbor hulks before falling out over three casks of phosphor-tar. Neither warlord trusted the other enough to post a sentry, leaving both camps blind to a third army.

Half a dozen leaking barrels of naval fire-tar lie mired in the mud between two slaughtered camps. Both free-companies swore the salvage belonged to their banner, proving greed outlives discipline even at the end of the world.

title: Admiral Kael's Copper Sheathing
summary: Act III relic codex unlocked on the scorched quarterdeck in Burning Harbor, detailing Admiral Kael's copper sheathing.
infobox: Examine the scorched copper hull-plates on Kael's quarterdeck in Burning Harbor.

p: To keep Harborwatch's fire-arrows from biting into his flagship's hull, Admiral Kael stripped the roofs of three coastal temples and nailed overlapping copper plates down to the waterline. Only an unarmored oak rudder left the vessel vulnerable to seawall catapults.

Thin sheets of hammered copper nailed below the waterline kept shipworms out and let naval hulls shrug off flaming pitch longer than bare oak. Scorched black now, the plates still gleam where boarding axes bit deep.

title: Heartland Ash-Stalkers
summary: Act IV creature codex unlocked near Highcrest bluff in Heartland March, examining the predators adapted to ash-drifts.
infobox: Inspect an ash-stalker carcass near Highcrest bluff in Heartland March.

p: Lean hounds with plates of fused volcanic glass along their spines, ash-stalkers bury themselves beneath black cinder drifts until boots crunch overhead. Their hides shed common broadheads unless struck at the soft sulfur-stained throat.

Lean highland beasts whose lungs developed thick mucus filters to breathe sulfurous air without coughing. Scouts check every carcass for burned collars, half expecting to recognize hounds that wandered south months ago.

title: Focusing Prisms of the Pass
summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked on the north crag in Shattered Beacons, detailing the crystal lenses of the signal grid.
infobox: Examine the shattered copper-bound crystal shards on the north crag in Shattered Beacons.

p: Cut from clear mountain quartz and bound in copper wire, these three crag prisms drink ambient storm-static to weave an impassable violet dome across the obsidian pass. Each prism is chained to a branded warden whose heartbeat keeps the arc steady.

Copper-bound quartz shards scattered across the granite still feel faintly warm hours after the tower collapsed. Linked together, three such prisms turned ordinary watch-fires into a lethal arcane curtain across the valley.

title: Greystone's Pumice Mortar
summary: Act IV place codex unlocked on Greystone's curtain wall in Besieged Wall, explaining the fortress's volcanic masonry.
infobox: Inspect the cracked parapet masonry on Greystone's curtain wall in Besieged Wall.

p: Built from light volcanic stone quarried near the heartland rim, Greystone Bastion was meant as a supply depot rather than a fortress. Its porous walls absorb small stones well enough, but demonic siege-engines chew the mortar into grey gravel within hours.

Highland masons mixed crushed volcanic pumice into their lime mortar so the walls would flex slightly during caldera tremors without shearing clean through. Even chipped by siege-golems, the grey stone refuses to crumble easily.

title: Malrik's Blindfold
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by inspecting a charred silk blindfold on the portal stairs in Flight of Malrik.
infobox: Examine the charred silk blindfold dropped on the portal stairs in Flight of Malrik.

p: Arch-Mage Malrik burned out his own eyes reading unshielded leyline codices, trading sight for the ability to feel stone seams through the soles of his boots. Even at a dead run up Ashveil Gorge, he could raise jagged obsidian walls without glancing back.

Collegium navigators sometimes bind their eyes with smoked silk to read raw ley-currents without being dazzled by volcanic glare. Dropped in haste on the upper steps of Ashveil Gorge, this scorched strip hints at how desperately its wearer ran.

title: Twenty-Heartbeat Mana-Cannons
summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked via a spiked bronze barrel inside the northern crag bastion during Twofold Assault.
infobox: Inspect a spiked bronze barrel inside the northern crag bastion in Twofold Assault.

p: Cast from blackened bronze and etched with containment runes, the twin crag cannons drink raw ley-salt to spit bolts of white fire down the citadel causeway. Their barrels glow cherry-red after each discharge, forcing gunners to wait twenty heartbeats before firing again.

Cast thick enough to survive twenty heartbeats of sustained arcane pressure before the breech turns cherry-red and threatens its own crew. Iron Pact gunners treat these bronze tubes with nervous respect, keeping wet sandbags piled beside every carriage.

title: The Lodestone Canyon
summary: Act IV place codex unlocked by checking iron filings on the middle portcullis in Gauntlet of Iron.
infobox: Check the iron filings clinging to the middle portcullis in Gauntlet of Iron.

p: Cliffs of natural magnetic iron squeeze the approach to the Citadel into a thirty-pace gut where loose daggers leap from sheaths and poorly riveted mail drags against the rock. Only heavy ash-wood tower-shields keep a column moving beneath the cliffside crossbow nests.

Natural lodestone veins run so dense through these canyon walls that loose belt-knives rattle in their sheaths as you march past. Quartermasters warn heavy infantry to double-check their boot nails before crossing the narrow bridge.

title: The Magma Moat Winches
summary: Act IV place codex unlocked by inspecting severed winch chains in the Center gatehouse of Outer Rampart.
infobox: Inspect the severed winch chains in the Center gatehouse in Outer Rampart.

p: Fed by a tapped volcanic fissure, a sluggish moat of glowing slag rings the Citadel's outer basalt wall. Its heavy iron drawbridge hangs on grease-packed counterweight winches inside the West and Center gatehouses, shielded from heat by thick oak shutters.

Massive iron chains dipped in tallow once raised the drawbridges over the glowing moat channels below the basalt wall. Seeing links thick as a blacksmith's wrist sheared clean through tells any sapper that the defenders expected no retreat.

title: Three-Roads Watch
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked via a scorched powder-convoy manifest on the western road in Three-Roads Siege.
infobox: Examine the scorched powder-convoy manifest on the western road in Three-Roads Siege.

p: Where three ash-choked wagon tracks meet outside the Citadel's outer moat, the vanguard threw up a ditch-and-gabion camp out of old powder barrels and volcanic rubble. Holding that crossroads meant fighting on three fronts with no wall at your back.

Half the ink is blistered away, yet the surviving tally shows kegs of blasting powder, spare axles, and winter salt bound for the highland junction. Whoever holds Three-Roads Watch holds the last supply artery feeding the caldera front.

title: The Silent Praetor Phalanx
summary: Act IV faction codex unlocked by inspecting a notched spear-butt beside the central dais in Threshold Choice.
infobox: Inspect a praetor's notched spear-butt beside the central dais in Threshold Choice.

p: Sworn to guard the geometric obsidian nave until the end of the age, the Arch-Warden's praetors had their tongues seared out at induction so no chant or plea could distract them from their spears. They fight without horn-calls, turning on stamped heel-clicks alone.

The Silent Praetor Phalanx answers no trumpet and speaks no challenge, standing motionless in pale armor until an intruder crosses the inner flagstones. Every deep notch along their spear-butts marks a century of unbroken subterranean duty.

title: The Crown of Order
summary: Act IV relic codex unlocked at the star-etched marble altar rim in Crown of Order, detailing an ancient symbol of law.
infobox: Examine the star-etched rim of the marble altar after completing Crown of Order.

p: Forged from cold meteoric silver rather than gold, the Crown of Order acts as a tuning fork for Thornvael's fractured leylines. When set upon the marble altar between two anchored seals, it binds wild magic back into rigid, predictable law—at the cost of mercy.

Pale stonework engraved with pre-schism star-geometry radiates a cold, austere stillness that quiets even the distant rumble of the caldera. Archivists debate whether the altar was built to preserve a realm or merely freeze it in place.

title: First Warden Ashkarath
summary: Act IV lore codex unlocked by inspecting a cracked slag breastplate near the Obsidian Throne in Ember Reckoning.
infobox: Inspect the cracked slag breastplate beside the Obsidian Throne in Ember Reckoning.

p: Once the chief engineer who sealed the primordial fire beneath the Citadel, Ashkarath stayed behind in the magma dark until cinder fused to his plates and his oath twisted into worship. He fed the throne room's twin conduit pillars for centuries rather than let the flame cool.

Before modern factions fought over tolls and salt, the First Warden stood watch over the furnace depths in armor poured from volcanic iron. The fractured plate bears no heraldry, only the scorched marks of an impossible vigil.

title: Tavern rumors
summary: Collection of forty frontier rumors overheard across the hubs, offering clues, gossip, and warnings from the Border.

list: Grok'tar's gnolls aren't raiding for cattle anymore—someone's paying them in fresh-stamped mint copper from before the fire.
Every third sack of barley taxed under Morvessa's Salt Tithe heads south past Alder Bridge, never toward the capital granaries.
Sawyers in Greywood found bog-iron ore sweating green slag near the old First Compact boundary stones.
Orlen refuses to bury anyone after sundown; he swears something in the Weeping Ossuary is spinning silk around the coffins.
Shaved silver groats turned up in the miller's lockbox—someone at the Border Mint clipped the dies six years ago.
Warden Hale hasn't slept since the Sunken Ford watch stopped sending tallies; he's hiring any blade that can hold a line.
Don't follow pale lights off the peat-road at dusk. Those aren't ford-scouts; mire wisps feed on stray Ley leaks.
The dwarven Undervault drains beneath Ravenwatch still carry dry air if you know which rusted sluice-wheel to turn.
Ashbrook Gatehouse was reinforced with ironwood beams last week—Morvessa expects a siege, not a tax audit.
Keep a spare flask of lamp oil if you enter the ossuary; fire clears Morvessa's silk-brood faster than cold steel.
Water-Seller Tull weighs every gill of boiled rainwater on apothecary scales—cross him and you drink alkali silt.
Someone chiseled reverse blood-wards into three of the twelve Quartz Wardstones; that's why the dust-squalls won't settle.
Lower-Parish clerks are binding indebted corpses with copper wire again to patrol the salt-vaults under Third-Dynasty law.
Sabik says the dune scarabs near the broken monoliths store enough static to knock a mailed knight off his boots.
Word from Deep Quarry is that chained miners broke into a Third-Dynasty probate vault—and nobody came back up the hoist.
Gorrathul hasn't opened Ironheart Bastion's twin sluice-gates in two winters. Some whisper his mountain cisterns silted completely dry.
Caravaneers found Morvessa's northern bullion chests stamped with Ironheart's seal—she was buying Gorrathul's silence with Border Mint silver.
If you march on the Gullet of Dunes, pack fire salts; Gorrathul's freeze aura stiffens bowstrings before you draw.
Chronicler Zahra claims the twelve wardstones aren't monuments at all—they're pressure anchors holding coastal rain over the plateau.
Never camp beside dry limestone slabs in Redmarsh; scale vipers wait beneath them for the warmth of a dying fire.
Lord Admiral Vesperion's Black Fleet isn't looting Oakhaven—he's burning every sea-going hull so no army can cross the southern straits.
Kors needs three barrels of refined whale-oil just to grease the drydock slipways before the fire-hulks drift into Harborwatch.
The Thermodynamic Conclave has been stringing copper wire along the sea-wall culverins—Sage Quillon calls it 'capacitance.'
When the tide drops at the Sunken Citadel, you can hear bronze frost-bells tolling under the drowned barbican.
The Bailey Truce barely holds; merchant captains want coin up front before risking a carrack against Vesperion's copper-sheeted rams.
Hourglass Spit got cut off at high water—half a vanguard company is still holding the ruined prism lighthouse.
Fen hexers from the Greywash marshes have been trading root-tonics for culverin powder; nobody knows which side they'll poison next.
Silt colossi still patrol the flooded canal locks, grinding drowned chains under their heels like it's still Year -156.
Surgeon Sera says glasswing cuts fester faster than ordinary steel—wrap every scratch in vinegar-soaked linen.
Vesperion's flagship carries a salt-corroded astrolabe locked due south toward the caldera plume. Take it, and we can sail.
Forgemaster Vok quenches star-iron blades in sulfur brine within four heartbeats—any slower and the metal turns brittle as glass.
Brother Elias and the Scorched Penitents blinded themselves voluntarily, claiming sightless eyes read the Anchor Seals' hum truer.
Arch-Mage Malrik's Ember Court is already climbing the Ashveil stairs with focusing prisms to crack the seventh Anchor Seal.
Ashkarath isn't a demon—he's the First Warden, four hundred years calcified, burning anyone who tries to uncap the magma core.
Three northern kings lost their heads at the Crossroads of Headless Kings for refusing the caldera maintenance tithe.
The Magnetic Narrows pull iron buckles straight toward the basalt cliffs—leave cheap scrap behind before crossing.
Anvilmaw smiths never leave their floor-fissures; listen for the hiss of their chest-furnaces before stepping into smoke.
Commander Rowan says the First Watch remnant still answers to the Crown of Order, provided you bring unbroken star-iron.
If Malrik shatters the seventh valve, northern harvests might thaw—or the whole continent could burn to vitrified slag.
Drink cold water while you still have it, captain. Above Three-Roads Watch, even the wind tastes of sulfur and iron.

p: Half of what you hear over watered ale in Thornwick or vinegar-brine in Redmarsh is drunken invention, and the other half might keep you alive tomorrow. Smart commanders listen quietly, buy one round, and check every rumor against the mud.

title: Act 1 Chronicle: Ash on the Southern Road
summary: At midnight, scouts returning from the alkali rim reported that the wells of Redmarsh had been sealed from within—and someone was already marching north to meet the column.

p: By dusk, the fires along Ashbrook's southern wall had burned down to a low, sour smudge against the twilight. The surviving townsfolk did not cheer when the last of Velen's siege companies broke up the valley; they loaded handcarts in grim silence, wrapping cracked icons and sacks of damp seed-corn in wool blankets. Captain Garrick stood by the splintered gatehouse counting notched tallies on a wooden slate, each mark a neighbor left beneath the turnip fields outside the ditch. Behind the column, Thornwick's watchtowers already looked small and irrelevant, their signal beacons gutters of gray smoke in the drizzle. Ahead lay the Desiccated Marches—a cracked bowl of alkali flats, dry riverbeds, and fortified cistern-towns where water was weighed on apothecary scales and strangers were judged by the dust on their boots. Fenwick poled his flat-bottomed barge one final time across the border ford before burning the mooring ropes, watching the current carry charred timbers south toward the salt flats. Nobody spoke of victory around the first night's cookfires. Everyone knew Ashbrook had not been saved; it had merely been emptied in time.
At midnight, scouts returning from the alkali rim reported that the wells of Redmarsh had been sealed from within—and someone was already marching north to meet the column.
Opens the Redmarsh caravan hub: water-rationing mechanics replace warmth, Tull and Zahra join as vendors and lore-brokers, and armored desert raiders replace border levies.

title: Act 2 Chronicle: The Salt Wind Below
summary: Before the vanguard even reached the coastal pines, black smoke began rising from the direction of Harborwatch—signals not of welcome, but of a fleet burning at anchor.

p: Ironheart Bastion did not fall with the roar of collapsing towers, but with the slow, metallic shriek of rusting sluice-wheels forced open after a generation of disuse. From the highest parapet of the forked peak, the victorious company looked down upon two very different worlds: behind them stretched the bleached ribs of Redmarsh, shimmering under a merciless white sun; ahead, beyond a jagged descent of switchbacks and wind-scoured scree, lay the gray-green haze of the Iron Coast. Quartermaster Bram spent the morning inventorying captured siege bolts and empty water barrels, muttering that the garrison had been defending ghosts and dried mud for years. Along the lower terraces, wounded mercenaries washed alkali grime from their faces in cold mountain condensation while Zahra copied faded hydraulic charts from the citadel's stone walls. The road down to Oakhaven was steep, narrow, and swept by salt gales that smelled of kelp, tar, and burning pine. For the first time in months, the boots of the army struck wet earth instead of cracked clay, though the distant boom of naval cannon across the bay warned that the sea offered no sanctuary.
Before the vanguard even reached the coastal pines, black smoke began rising from the direction of Harborwatch—signals not of welcome, but of a fleet burning at anchor.
Unlocks Oakhaven port and coastal routes: naval artillery hazards, shipwright upgrades from Kors, healer triage contracts from Sera, and amphibious privateer enemies.

title: Act 3 Chronicle: The Fleet Has Sailed. The Sword Remains.
summary: Marshal Veyra wiped salt brine and black ash from her cutlass and stared toward the burning peaks: 'We have bought them their morning... now let us march into the night.'

p: The choking smoke over Harborwatch thinned beneath the cold wind off the Western Sea as Lord-Captain Korvus sank beneath the black surf with his twin anchors. Beyond the scorched seawall, the white sails of the evacuation armada—plated in black ironstone by Miner Gorin's freed smiths and caulked by the shipwrights pulled from the drowning tidal vaults—shrank into pinpricks against the slate-gray horizon, carrying Thornwick's survivors, Chief Healer Sera's wounded, seed-grain, and histories safely past the rim. The slipways lay utterly empty, only severed mooring ropes swaying in the black water. Standing beside Harbor Marshal Veyra, Bailiff Aldric, and the last bloodied veterans on the eastern pier, you turned your back to the quiet ocean. Fifty leagues inland to the east, the Obsidian Caldera had torn completely open in a pillar of white fire and shattered obsidian.
Marshal Veyra wiped salt brine and black ash from her cutlass and stared toward the burning peaks: 'We have bought them their morning... now let us march into the night.'
Unlocks Highcrest Citadel: Tier 5 meteoric tempering from Weaponsmith Elda, pre-calamity truths from Archivist Orla, and the final reckoning in the Obsidian Caldera.

title: Act 4 Chronicle: The Reckoning of Thornvael
summary: Across four scarred provinces from Thornwick to the Obsidian Peaks, a new age dawned over a continent that had survived the end of the world.

p: In the silence beneath the sundered Infernal Sanctuary, the four-act tragedy of Thornvael reached its final balance—from Morvessa's Salt Tithe at the Border Fords and Gorrathul's dry cisterns atop Ironheart, to the burning piers of Harborwatch and the Threshold Chamber beneath the volcano. Highcrest Citadel fell quiet as Marshal Vance, Harbor Marshal Veyra, and Archivist Orla stood by the gate watching the horizon shift: whether cooled by the snapping of Arch-Warden Korrath's necrotic tether so the western sails might return to a fragile living morning, or sealed in obsidian glass beneath the blazing Crown of Thorns and Cinder claimed from Ember Overlord Vorak's kiln.
Across four scarred provinces from Thornwick to the Obsidian Peaks, a new age dawned over a continent that had survived the end of the world.
Campaign Complete — Explore both Threshold endings (Crown of Order / Ember Reckoning) or challenge Nightmare & Hell difficulties.

title: Canonical Chronicle — Act I — The Border Fords
summary: Canonical Act I chronicle triggered at Blood at the Ford, opening the frontier campaign across the wet northern border.

sections.h: Funeral Pyres along the Border Fords
p: Cold, relentless rain lashes the swollen timber crossings of the frontier, washing soot and viscera into the gray rapids. Frontier watchtowers have burned to blackened stumps, their halberdiers butchered where they stood by howling gnoll war-packs. As iron crows wheel over the mire, your veterans tighten their harness—beyond these shallows lies a frontier forsaken by the gods.
“Steel remembers what bone forgets: on this border, mercy is only a slower way to bleed.”

Behind the soot-blackened bastions of Thornwick Keep, scarred sellswords, hooded border rangers, and renegade battle-mages huddle over iron braziers. Gold cannot resurrect the dead, yet the Imperial writ is stamped in crimson wax: force the sunken crossings, cleave through the highland horde, and purge the ancient evil awakening in the dark.
“Twelve blades against a wilderness of fangs. If we break, the bells of Thornwick toll for an empty keep.”

sections.h: ACT I COMPLETE — The Threshold of Ashbrook Gate
p: The iron doors of Ashbrook groan open. Behind you lies the wet, bleeding North—free from the tithe, yet shadowed by Morvessa’s dying warning. Ahead, the sky burns the color of old rust above the Redmarsh Wastes.
The North is free. Yet as the warm sulfur wind strikes my face, I wonder if I just killed the only soul who had a plan to stop the fire.

Rain drums steadily against the palisade timbers of Thornwick while gnoll horns echo across the Alder shallows. What begins as a desperate border skirmish soon pulls the Vanguard Company into a tangled ledger of burned mints and unpaid tithes.

title: Canonical Chronicle — Act II — The Desiccated Marches
summary: Canonical Act II chronicle triggered at Redmarsh Border, marking the march from sunken mires into scorching alkali wastes.

p: The brackish swamps recede into cracked salt flats littered with the calcified ribcages of primeval beasts. A forgotten imperial highway cuts through the alkaline silt, its runic mile-markers chipped and stained by blood-cultists. Above, a merciless copper sun hangs like an open furnace, baking the dead and drawing venomous things from subterranean fissures.
“The salt bites at cracked lips and rusted mail alike. Out here, even water tastes of ash and ancient slaughter.”

sections.h: The Furnace Winds of the Dune Sea
p: Gales of stinging quartz and sulfur howl between cyclopean basalt pillars that once held back the underworld. Across the shifting dunes, dune scourges and burrowing abominations stalk the column, drawn by the thrum of desecrated elemental shrines. Two sunken passes pierce the canyon wall—each flanked by weeping effigies of forgotten kings.
“The dunes bury crowns and beggars without distinction. Keep your shields locked; the wind itself carries teeth.”

sections.h: ACT II COMPLETE — The Empty Mountain
p: The great iron sluice-gates groan open onto a subterranean cathedral engineered for three million barrels of glacial water. Instead, dry wind whistles across a silent canyon of cracked red silt—the glaciers died fifty years ago.
The well is dry. The road leads to the sea.

Beyond Ashbrook Gate the northern grass dies abruptly into blinding red clay and salt-crusted flats. Caravans creak south on the promise of mountain water, guarded by mercenaries who trust their canteens far more than imperial seals.

title: Canonical Chronicle — Act III — Descent into the Sunless Deeps
summary: The Iron Coast, The Drowned Citadel & The Rearguard of Burning Harbor

sections.h: The Dry Cisterns & The Road to Oakhaven
p: Behind the forked ridge of Ironheart, Gorrathul’s mountain cisterns stood revealed as dry red silt—a fifty-year mirage kept alive at spearpoint. Turning west from the salt wastes, your column descends through towering ironwood groves toward Oakhaven and Harborwatch, where Harbor Marshal Veyra and Master Shipwright Kors race against tectonic tremors to hammer together the last evacuation caravels.
“When a continent catches fire, men run to the sea. But every hull has a waterline—and not everyone on the pier will ever board a ship.”

sections.h: The Rearguard of the Iron Coast
p: Storm-lashed cliffs ring the sunless sea-caves of the Drowned Citadel and the roaring riverlocks above Harborwatch. Between predatory warbands tearing at each other for boarding manifests and the primeval Elder Juggernaut stirring in tectonic agony, Chief Healer Sera tends the broken in the glade while you stand as the Shield of the Departing—buying every minute of hull-caulking in blood.
“Hold the riverlocks, hold the infirmary, hold the final pier. We do not fight for gold anymore; we fight so their sails clear the rim.”

sections.h: ACT III COMPLETE — The Fleet Has Sailed
p: White sails vanish into the western mist, carrying Thornvael’s children and memory beyond the rim. On the bloodstained flagstones of Harborwatch, you turn your back to the sea and face the incandescent violet pillar tearing open the eastern sky.
We have given them their dawn. Now, before the Caldera boils the ocean itself, we march into the night.

title: Canonical Chronicle — Act IV — Gates of the Infernal Sanctuary
summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle triggered at Heartland March, introducing the final ascent into the Obsidian Caldera.

sections.h: The Empty Slipways & The Obsidian Caldera
p: Behind Harborwatch’s scorched breakwater, the white sails of the evacuation armada shrink into pinpricks against the western mist—safe beyond the rim. Turning your back on the ocean beside Marshal Veyra and Marshal Vance, you march fifty leagues east along the cracked basalt highway into the Obsidian Caldera, where the Iron Pact fortifies the Infernal Sanctuary above rivers of white-hot slag.
“The fleet has sailed. Their dawn is on the water. We have bought them their morning—now let us march into the night.”

sections.h: Highcrest Citadel & The Threshold of Will
p: At Highcrest Citadel, Archivist Orla decodes the final ledgers linking Morvessa’s northern Salt Tithe to the Iron Pact’s treason, while Weaponsmith Elda tempers meteoric steel against volcanic ash. Beyond Greystone Bastion, Ashveil Gorge, and the Gauntlet of Iron waits the Threshold Chamber—where Arch-Warden Korrath’s petrified law and Ember Overlord Vorak’s living kiln demand an answer: what deserves to rise from the ashes of a dying world?
“No one left is asking us to hold a bridge. At the furnace heart of the earth, we decide who holds the right to name the dawn.”

Behind the vanguard lies the gray Western Sea; ahead rises a horizon lit by sulfur vents and black basalt peaks. In the thin, ash-choked air of the highlands, old grievances burn away until only iron and resolve remain.

title: Threshold Chronicle — Victory — The Purging of Thornvael
summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle for the Path of Order, recording the culmination of the Threshold trial in Crown of Order.

p: With a chime of sundered granite, the necrotic tether snaps. Molten fissures cool into harmless black basalt as clean mountain winds sweep the Caldera, and far to the west, the returning sails of the fleet turn homeward.
The nightmare is broken. Our hands are stained with ash, but the sky—for the first time in an age—is blue.

Golden morning light spills across the emerald hills of Thornwick and the healing shallows of the Border Fords. Far to the west, the returning sails of the evacuation armada catch a clean breeze, turning homeward toward a shore that no longer burns. Notched swords and dented shields hang above rebuilding hearths—and the quiet saga of the rearguard who stayed behind to buy the world another morning echoes through generations of hard-won peace.
“The empire was stone and silence; the dawn is scarred, imperfect, and free. Let a living world learn how to keep it.”

Cold marble light meets the roaring heat of the caldera as an ancient standard of law is tested to its breaking point. Whatever emerges from the quiet vault will decide whether Thornvael's scarred valleys ever know a calm morning again.

title: Threshold Chronicle — Alternative Ending — Rise of the Dark Sovereign
summary: Canonical Act IV chronicle for the Path of Ember, recording the fiery culmination of the Threshold trial in Ember Reckoning.

sections.h: Claiming the Crown of Thorns and Cinder
p: Vorak sinks into the magma, yet the Crown of Thorns and Cinder waits upon the obsidian altar. Lifting it, the hero bends every leyline of the continent to a single, unbreakable sovereign will.
Let them call it tyranny. Beneath the rule of steel and cinder, no storm, no traitor, and no god will ever break these borders again.

sections.h: The Iron Throne of the New Age
p: Standards of crimson velvet and smoking steel rise over every stronghold from the Border Fords to the Obsidian Peaks. The Caldera obeys its new master, sealing its fissures into an impregnable fortress of black glass. Man, beast, and risen dead kneel in hushed, terrified awe before the Sovereign of Embers and Shadow—pacifying Thornvael at last under an iron dominion that will never falter, never bleed, and never fall.
“Let them call it tyranny. Beneath the peace of steel and cinder, no storm, no traitor, and no god will ever break these borders again.”

Where pale statutes fail, raw volcanic fire offers a harsher, simpler answer forged in white-hot steel and absolute will. Stepping toward the furnace altar means trading fragile peace for a dominion that refuses to bend.

title: Act 1 Epilogue: Cold Iron at the Fords
summary: With the toll-brigands broken and the river crossings cleared, flat-bottomed barges finally resumed hauling timber and salted pike into Thor

p: With the toll-brigands broken and the river crossings cleared, flat-bottomed barges finally resumed hauling timber and salted pike into Thornwick. Yet the victory brought no royal relief—only tax-assessors arriving under heavy escort to audit the salvaged granaries. Along Alder Bridge, blacksmiths melted down captured spearheads into plowshares and wagon-tires while widows patched the palisades before autumn rains swelled the banks once more. The Border Fords stood quiet at last, though every watchman knew the real rot lay deeper south where the river spilled into Redmarsh.

title: Act 2 Epilogue: Embers Over the Black Peat
summary: After the false lanterns went dark and the Mire-Cult altars lay shattered in the silt, peat-cutters returned cautiously to the raised boardw

p: After the false lanterns went dark and the Mire-Cult altars lay shattered in the silt, peat-cutters returned cautiously to the raised boardwalks of Redmarsh. Quicklime trenches were sealed and drained, though green marsh-gas still bubbled through the reeds whenever thunder rolled across the dikes. Without tax-wagons or royal garrisons to enforce old decrees, the surviving apothecaries and ferrymen forged their own rough truce, trading bitter-root salves for dry grain from the north. Behind you, the bog slowly swallowed the ruins, leaving only bleached cairns above the black water.

title: Act 3 Epilogue: Empty Slipways, Unbroken Rearguard
summary: Once Lord-Captain Korvus fell into the churning harbor surf and the last caravel caught the offshore breeze, Harborwatch's bells fell silent

p: Once Lord-Captain Korvus fell into the churning harbor surf and the last caravel caught the offshore breeze, Harborwatch's bells fell silent. With the evacuation fleet carrying Thornvael's families, seed-grain, and histories past the Western Rim, Marshal Veyra and the surviving rearguard turned inland along the cracked obsidian road toward Highcrest Citadel.

title: Act 4 Epilogue: The Legacy of the Threshold
summary: When the roaring furnace of the Obsidian Caldera finally fell still, the long ledger opened in the rain at Thornwick was closed at last. Whe

p: When the roaring furnace of the Obsidian Caldera finally fell still, the long ledger opened in the rain at Thornwick was closed at last. Whether by the clean mountain winds of the Crown Vault or the unyielding fire of the Furnace Heart, Thornvael stepped out of the shadow of extinction into the age forged by its rearguard.

title: Ending: Warrior (sovereign)
summary: Act IV Warrior campaign epilogue reflecting how a frontline commander shapes the Border after the Threshold.

p: When the last Anchor Seal cooled into brittle grey slag, no choirs sang from the cracked dome of the Obsidian Dais. The warrior simply unbuckled a dented pauldron, sat upon the lowest basalt step, and let the silence settle into joints that had ache-warned of rain across four provinces.

In the weeks that followed, Thornvael was measured not by prophetic hymns, but by supply manifests, mended bridge-pilings, and muster-rolls paid in weighed silver. Ironcamp's trip-hammers shifted from siege-mauls to plowshares and sluice-gears, while garrisons from Thornwick to Harborwatch learned that a gatehouse held by well-fed pikemen needs no divine miracle.

The Obsidian Throne remained cold and empty behind a locked iron grate—guarded not by zealots, but by a rotating watch of tired veterans who knew that every crown is just another heavy helmet someone eventually has to take off.

list: He traded the notched broadsword for a surveyor's plumb-line at Alder Bridge, collecting a modest pension and complaining loudly whenever spring floods soaked his knees.
She drafted the new border fortification charter in Oakhaven, personally inspecting every rivet along the seawall until masons learned to fear her calipers more than winter gales.

p: A soldier who has held muddy bridges, salt ditches, and burning piers learns to measure peace in solid walls and dry granaries. When the horns finally fall silent, the iron weight of command still rests squarely on broad shoulders.

title: Ending: Archer (horizon)
summary: Act IV Archer campaign epilogue tracing the frontier path of a marksman after the caldera campaign concludes.

p: With the caldera's ash-plume thinning into pale coastal mist, the archer stood at the cracked parapet of the Threshold and checked the wind—steady sou'west, smelling of kelp and cooling iron for the first time in a generation.

Rather than claim a seat among the bickering councilors of Oakhaven or the rebuilt halls of Thornwick, the company disbanded quietly at the crossroads, each scout carrying a full purse and clear sightlines across four pacified provinces. Toll-towers reopened along the Redmarsh salt-roads without brass-knuckled bailiffs, and foresters walked Greywood again without losing thumbs to royal wardens.
Years later, travelers along the border fords still swore they caught the faint snap of a waxed yew bowstring whenever brigands grew bold at dusk—though no banner ever flew above the treeline.

list: He rebuilt the watch-platform above the Redmarsh salt-road, charging two coppers for safe passage and keeping a slate of charcoal tallies that never once failed to balance.
She vanished north into the Greywood timberlands with a dry quiver and a pouch of pre-Schism silver, leaving Oakhaven's council three unsigned maps of every drafty gap in their new walls.

p: Scouts and bowmen never sit comfortably behind palace curtains once the roads clear. With the smoke lifting off the passes, a keen eye naturally turns toward the far ridgeline, checking the wind and counting what lies beyond.

title: Ending: Mage (equilibrium)
summary: Act IV Mage campaign epilogue detailing how an arcanist balances the fractured ley-lines of the realm.

p: Once the Obsidian Dais stopped inhaling ambient heat, the mage knelt beside the fractured conduit pillars with a brass caliper and a water-stained notebook, recording the exact rate at which Thornvael's ley-currents returned to thermodynamic equilibrium.

Under the new charter drafted between Oakhaven's towers and Ironcamp's foundries, magic ceased to be hoarded as aristocratic liturgy and became an audited civic craft. Grounded copper lattices protected coastal lighthouses from squalls, regulated sluice-valves kept Redmarsh cisterns from boiling dry, and every apprentice learned that a misplaced syllable is merely a sloppy pressure leak.
The Capital Collegium sent three formal invitations offering reinstatement and a velvet chair; all three were returned unopened, stamped with a dry correction regarding their plumbing schematics.

list: He established a provincial observatory atop the Quartz Plateau, publishing twelve volumes on ley-conservation while complaining ceaselessly about sand in his inkwell.
She assumed oversight of the Thornwick Mint and Oakhaven's galvanic works, ensuring every silver crown weighed true to the grain and every furnace vented cleanly.

p: Collegium formulas rarely survive contact with a dying continent, yet someone must recalibrate the wards once the tremors subside. Chalk, copper wire, and quiet patience become the tools of a new, hard-won equilibrium.

title: Ending: Necromancer (probate)
summary: Act IV Necromancer campaign epilogue chronicling how a clerk of bone and debt settles the realm's final accounts.

p: When the Anchor Seals shattered, ten thousand frozen oaths thawed simultaneously across the obsidian nave—a silent, pressing crowd of First-Watch wardens, drowned sailors, and border levies awaiting the signature that would release them from centuries of unpaid watch.

Dipping a bone-nibbed pen into grey caldera ash, the necromancer spent seven days and seven nights auditing the great mortuary roll. Every broken promise was witnessed, every illegitimate tax lien voided in red ink, and every indentured spirit formally discharged with a stamped brass token.

Thornvael grew quiet afterward—not the hollow quiet of a graveyard, but the clean stillness of a ledger balanced to the final copper, where the dead sleep untaxed and the living inherit no debts they did not sign.

list: He reopened the lower-parish registry in Thornwick, serving as public probate arbiter where no magistrate dared forge a widow's will while his bone-awl rested on the desk.
She returned to the coastal scriptorium above Harborwatch, keeping the tide-bell polished and witnessing sailors' vows so no soul need ever walk the shingle unrecorded.

p: War leaves behind more than broken walls—it leaves thousands of unclosed ledgers and restless dead waiting for a proper signature. Armed with wax seal and brass scale, the probate arbiter finally brings order to the silent rolls.

title: New Game+ (Second Cycle)
summary: Modifiers and chronicle lines unlocked after completing Act IV.

list: The ash settles, yet the ledger turns back to page one—heavier ink, sharper steel.
Thornwick's rain still leaks through the same rotten eaves, though your boots know every puddle.
They rebuilt the tollhouse at the Sunken Ford, and the gnolls brought thicker iron this season.
Even the crows along Alder Bridge recognize your banner before the first horn blows.
The Anchor Seals remember the hand that broke them; this time they burn hotter.
New cycle, old debts—let us see how much silver you can carry before the mud claims it.
Compounded Salt-Tithe: Enemy armor +25% and physical damage +20%; gold drops increased by +40%.
Caldera Updrafts: All fire and astral hazards deal +35% damage; unique drop rate doubled.
Unsettled Probate: Slain non-boss enemies have a 20% chance to rise once as hollow skeletons.
Rationed Canteens: Potion healing reduced by 25%, but camp rest restores full stamina and mana.
Veteran Levy: Every encounter spawns +1 elite champion carrying guaranteed Tier 4–5 salvage.
Corrosive Brine: Equipment repair costs +50%, while weapon armor penetration increases by +15%.
Overcharged Lattice: Spell damage and mana costs both increase by +30% across all schools.
Tightened Hourglass: Boss enrage timers reduced by 45 seconds; boss XP and relic drops +50%.
Perpetual Fen-Mist: Squad vision radius reduced by 2 tiles; flanking critical damage +35%.
Brand of the Dais: Hero takes +15% incoming damage but radiates +20% all-damage aura to mercenaries.

title: The Tollhouse Strongbox
summary: Act I side quest from Captain Garrick in Thornwick, rewarding gold and experience for recovering a lost tollhouse strongbox.

p: Before the gnolls fired the river crossing, Collector Harlon locked three months of border tariffs inside a weighted iron strongbox and kicked it into the reeds. Sergeant Garrick needs that silver to pay the militia's back-wages before they desert. Clear the Briar Hound packs scavenging the shallows and drag the box out of the mud.

Choice A: Hand the sealed strongbox to Garrick (+1 militia morale, unlocks cheaper mercs in Thornwick). Choice B: Pry the lock open with Old Fenwick and split the silver (+300 extra gold now, but Garrick's militia starts 'Alder Bridge' with 20% less HP).

Garrick hates losing payroll silver almost as much as he hates losing ground to gnolls. Somewhere in the burned timbers near the river crossing sits a heavy ironbound box whose padlock refuses to yield to ordinary bandits.

title: Bile of the Fen
summary: Act I side quest from Alchemist Marta in Thornwick, paying gold and experience for harvesting potent marsh bile.

p: Widow Marta's supply of marsh-antidote has run dry, and a dozen scouts from Bren's column are swelling up from poisoned iron arrowheads. She needs fresh gas-bladders harvested from Mire Wisps before their internal fire goes cold. Wade into the willow sinks and bring back intact specimens.

Choice A: Give all 6 bladders to Marta to save the scouts (Marta reduces potion prices by 20% permanently). Choice B: Sell the volatile bladders to the garrison sappers for fire-pots (+250 gold and +1 Fireball scroll, but 3 scouts die and Bren refuses to speak to you).

Marta's apothecary shelves are nearly bare, and wounded levies need poultices that actually bite back against bog-fever. She needs fresh, foul ingredients scraped from creatures that prefer to keep their insides to themselves.

title: The Broken Picket
summary: Act I side quest offered by Captain Garrick in Thornwick, awarding gold and experience for clearing a compromised picket line.

p: Four border watchmen abandoned the outer watchtower during the Ravenwatch siege, leaving their comrades to be butchered by Thorn Boars. They are currently hiding in a hunter's blind near the pine line, guarded by feral packs. Hunt down the Thorn Boars around the blind and deal with the deserters according to martial law.

Choice A: Execute the deserters on the spot as Garrick ordered (grants +2 Body elixir, reveals Garrick's nephew secret). Choice B: Conscript them into your vanguard for the Sunken Sanctum (you gain 2 free disposable spearman mercs for the next mission, but Garrick withholds the gold reward).

A forward watch-post went silent before dawn without firing a single flare or blowing a horn. Garrick wants boots on the trail to find out what broke the line and sweep the ridge clean before raiders dig in.

title: Night Cargo
summary: Act I side quest from Ferryman Fenwick in Thornwick, offering gold and experience for tracking missing river freight.

p: A flat-bottomed sulfur barge grounded on the gravel shoals north of the ford three nights ago. Flintbacks have already nested on the deck, cracking the casks of river-salt open with their stone hides. Clear the beasts off the hull before the whole bend goes up in orange smoke.

Choice A (Return the salvaged sulfur casks to npc-fenwick-ferryman): Fenwick smuggles them upriver; in Act 3, npc-kors-shipwright in town-oakhaven charges -20% on hull and shield repairs. Choice B (Dump the casks into the river to deny everyone powder): m08-alder-bridge has 3 fewer cinderling spawns, but npc-fenwick-ferryman raises river-crossing fees by +25% and mutters about 'pious drowners of good freight'.
Fenwick knows every snag and sandbar on the Alder, which is why he smells foul play when a loaded flatboat vanishes in calm fog. Someone is moving contraband off the books under cover of the curfew.

title: The Quartermaster's Ledger
summary: Act I side quest from Smith Hobb in Thornwick, rewarding gold and experience for retrieving a missing supply book.

p: Hobb forged forty iron axle-pins and twelve billhooks on militia credit, and the clerk who carried the tallow-skin ledger bolted into the Greywood when the vanguard split. Without those tallies, the garrison captain refuses to pay a single copper. Pull the oilskin ledger out of the wrecked supply cart before the mites chew it to pulp.

Choice A (Give the unaltered ledger to npc-hobb-smith): Hobb gets his payout and unlocks tier-2 weapon tempering at -15% cost in town-thornwick, while npc-garrick-captain loses face and gives no bonus rations before m09-ironhide-hunt. Choice B (Sell the ledger to npc-garrick-captain to cover up his requisition embezzlement): You gain +90 extra gold immediately, but in Act 2 npc-bram-quartermaster in town-redmarsh recognizes the forged tallies and increases his shop prices by +15%.

Without a stamped tally, Hobb cannot prove how much pig-iron the Salt Tithe took and how much the bailiffs simply pocketed. Finding the lost ledger in the mud could keep the town forge running another month.

title: Glass in the Thicket
summary: Act I side quest from Alchemist Marta in Thornwick, granting gold and experience for gathering vitrified glass shards.

p: Marta's apprentice went out to tap birch-tar near the oldwatch cairns and came back with three translucent crystal shards wedged in his collarbone. A swarm of Cinderlings has nested in the dead ash trees above the road, blinding scouts with refracted glare. Bring down the brood-leaders so their glass cores can be ground into sight-salve.

Choice A (Let npc-marta-alchemist distill the cores into militia eye-drops): Ranged mercenaries gain +5 accuracy during m11-ashbrook-retreat, and Marta greets you as 'the one who kept our eyes open'. Choice B (Grind the crystal dust into trade-poison for yourself): Marta's apprentice loses sight in one eye and she refuses to brew cold-resistance draughts for the rest of Act 1, though your party gains +120 gold from contraband buyers.

Strange green splinters have been turning up in the brush near the old kilns, sharp enough to slice through boot leather. Marta suspects the fused slag holds residual ward-charge useful for stabilizing field tonics.

title: The Canyon Audit
summary: Act II side quest from Quartermaster Bram in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for accounting lost canyon supplies.

p: Three mule-trains of salted mutton and cold-iron arrowheads vanished between the Twin Passes and the marsh palisade. Bram suspects the drivers staged an ambush and sold the crates to desert nomads, though the canyon floor is crawling with Pale Burrowers. Escort Bram's bonded tally-clerk to the overturned wagons in the gorge so he can count the branding-irons on the dead mules.

Choice A (Report the drivers' desertion honestly to npc-bram-quartermaster): Bram hangs the surviving driver's brother; his shop stock expands with heavy bolts at -10% price, but in m20-deep-quarry 2 extra sand-raider mercs join the enemy side for revenge. Choice B (Falsify the audit and blame the burrowers): The driver's kin slips you 180 gold in hush-money, but npc-bram-quartermaster runs short on iron and removes all shield items from his store.

Bram refuses to write off three missing wagon-loads of salt-pork without seeing the splinters himself. Someone has to hike into the sun-baked passes, count the wreckage, and drag back whatever the sand raiders left behind.

title: Rubbings in Blood
summary: Act II side quest from Scholar Zahra in Redmarsh, paying gold and experience for copying defaced wardstone inscriptions.

p: When the wardstone ruptured, the peat bog drained enough to expose three pre-dynastic boundary steles carved with marsh-binding glyphs. Zahra needs charcoal-and-tallow rubbings of the inscriptions before the rising mire-water and Spore Matrons dissolve the limestone. Reach the three sunken steles in the outer fen and hold the ground long enough to press the parchment.

Choice A (Give all three rubbings to npc-zahra-scholar): She deciphers the marsh hexes, reducing enemy witch-doctor curse duration in m19-hexer-capture, and in Act 4 npc-elias-penitent in town-ironcamp recognizes her annotations and shares his secret dialogue early. Choice B (Burn the third stele's rubbing as demanded by a cornered witch-doctor in exchange for his fetish-cache): You receive +250 gold, but m19-hexer-capture spawns 1 additional spore-matron and Zahra calls you an illiterate grave-robber.

Zahra cannot fix the plateau's fractured monoliths without knowing the exact reverse glyphs carved into their bases. Getting close enough to take clean rubbings means wading through crackling static and irritable desert beasts.

title: The Bitter Well
summary: Act II side quest from Water-Seller Tull in Redmarsh, awarding gold and experience for investigating a fouled oasis well.

p: Tull's stone cistern at the edge of the landing has turned thick and green, smelling of copper and boiled maggots. A pair of Lantern Eels burrowed up through the broken limestone filter-grate and are laying shock-eggs in the town's only sweet-water reserve. Kill the eels in the cistern vaults before Tull is forced to sell boiled bog-water at famine prices.

Choice A (Clean the cistern grate and flush the eggs): npc-tull-water-seller lowers potion and flask prices in town-redmarsh by -20%, and in Act 3 npc-sera-healer in town-oakhaven receives clean water barrels, granting your party +15 max HP during m27-field-infirmary. Choice B (Harvest the intact shock-eggs for alchemical sale): Tull's water remains brackish, his prices rise by +20%, and 2 extra maggot-swarm packs appear in m21-lean-garrison, though you pocket +300 gold from lightning-salts.

Tull's customers are already paying silver for muddy brine, and now the main aquifer tastes like copper rot and toad-bile. If the source of the taint is not cleared soon, Redmarsh will have a riot before sundown.

title: Granary Smokers
summary: Act II side quest from Quartermaster Bram in Redmarsh, offering gold and experience for stopping arsonists targeting grain.

p: After the granary raid, half the barley silos are infested with Ruin Mites chewing through the foundation mortar. Bram's laborers set up peat-smoke braziers to suffocate the swarm in the lower vaults, but the smell of roasting chitin draws bog predators out of the reeds. Defend the four smoking braziers at the silo doors until the vaults are purged.

Choice A (Vent the silos early to save the trapped convict laborers coughing inside): Two laborers survive and join the garrison, removing 2 dune-lurker ambushes in m21-lean-garrison, but 30% of the grain spoils and Bram deducts 80 gold from your pay. Choice B (Keep the heavy iron doors barred until every mite is dead): You get the full 310 gold plus a 90 gold bonus, but npc-bram-quartermaster's dialogue turns grim as the town eats smoked grain that smells of dead prisoners.

Dry timber stilts and alkali dust burn like tinder if a single fire-pot lands under the granary floor. Bram wants the raiders' pitch-runners hunted down in the ditches before Redmarsh's last flour sacks go up in smoke.

title: Canopic Tar
summary: Act II side quest from Scholar Zahra in Redmarsh, rewarding gold and experience for recovering Third-Dynasty bitumen.

p: Deep quarry blasting broke into an older salt-brick burial gallery where Crypt Embalmers still tend rows of bitumen-sealed jars. Zahra wants four jars of unspoiled funerary pitch to seal her parchment crates against the marsh rot. Slay the embalmers guarding the lower gallery before they wake the rest of the alcoves.

Choice A (Deliver the sealed jars to npc-zahra-scholar): She preserves her treatise and teaches your mage/healer +10 poison_res permanently. Choice B (Crack the jars to loot the gold tongue-plates inside the viscera): You gain +220 gold, but breaking the seals releases necrotic fumes that cause 2 additional greater-mummy enemies to spawn in Act 3's m28-sunken-citadel.

Ancient embalmers sealed their salt-vaults with a mineral pitch far tougher than modern wagon-grease. Zahra needs fresh samples from the sunken quays to test whether it can insulate cracked quartz conduits.

title: Empty Waterskins
summary: Act II side quest from Water-Seller Tull in Redmarsh, granting gold and experience for salvaging lost caravan canteens.

p: The fleeing column from the south ridges abandoned their brass water-wagons in the dry scrub when the Dune Beasts struck. Tull knows those brass tanks are worth more than the mules that pulled them, and he wants the copper valves stripped before Sand Raiders haul them off. Collect six stamped brass valves from the wrecked wagons along the ridge trail.

Choice A (Leave two full water-tanks intact for the stragglers hiding in the rocks): You return with fewer valves (-100 gold), but the surviving scouts mark enemy paths for you, removing 3 claw-viper ambushes in m23-fork-of-spears. Choice B (Drain every tank to strip all six valves quickly): Tull pays the full reward and offers a discount on mana flasks, but the stragglers die of thirst and rise as 3 hollow-knight enemies in m23-fork-of-spears.

Out on the alkali flats, a stitched goatskin without leaks is worth more than a decorative dagger. Tull pays good coin for intact skins recovered from stranded convoys before the desert sun bakes them brittle.

title: The Triage Wagon
summary: Act III side quest from Healer Sera in Oakhaven, paying gold and experience for rescuing a stranded medical cart.

p: Sera's heavy ambulance wagon is bogged down in axle-deep shingle half a mile outside the field infirmary, surrounded by Cinderlings drawn to fever-heat of the wounded. Inside are twelve amputees from the sundered ranks and all of Oakhaven's willow-bark laudanum. Defend the wagon until the ox-team can be hitched and dragged behind the palisade.
