p: Tilted spiral stair climbing above a half-submerged First-Empire sea-fortress.
Atlantic breakers thunder through cracked embrasures twenty feet below.

title: Hourglass Shingle Spit
summary: Narrow gravel bar linking Iron-Gate Watchtower to the mainland at low water.

p: Narrow gravel bar linking Iron-Gate Watchtower to the mainland at low water.
White surf climbs steadily over shrinking dry stone with every wave.

title: High-Orchard Terraces
summary: Ash-choked apple groves terraced below a pale chalk watchtower.

p: Ash-choked apple groves terraced below a pale chalk watchtower.
Gnarled black trunks creak in sea fog, hung with whispering skulls.

title: Riverlock Capstan Island
summary: Stone redoubt wedged between roaring canal floodgates and iron counterweights.

p: Stone redoubt wedged between roaring canal floodgates and iron counterweights.
Massive bronze gears groan under fifty tons of backed-up river water.

title: Baron Vane's Vault Lift
summary: Iron-grated counterweight hoist descending from the manor hall into sea-caves.

p: Iron-grated counterweight hoist descending from the manor hall into sea-caves.
Gold ingots lie spilled beside smashed strongboxes and dropped halberds.

title: Harborwatch Culverin Wall
summary: Smoke-blackened stone seawall bristling with bronze coastal artillery above burning piers.

p: Smoke-blackened stone seawall bristling with bronze coastal artillery above burning piers.
Tarred hulls roar like floating furnaces across the choppy black bay.

title: Obsidian Landing Coves
summary: Crescent beaches of crushed volcanic glass choked with drifting grey ash.

p: Crescent beaches of crushed volcanic glass choked with drifting grey ash.
Yellow sulfur crust steams ten paces inland from the boiling surf.

title: Highcrest Redoubt
summary: Jagged basalt plateau overlooking the scorched imperial highway into the caldera.

p: Jagged basalt plateau overlooking the scorched imperial highway into the caldera.
Freshly dug trenches and iron stakes anchor the vanguard's first camp.

title: West Focusing Crag
summary: Lightning-lashed obsidian spire housing a humming violet capacitor prism.

p: Lightning-lashed obsidian spire housing a humming violet capacitor prism.
Blue static arcs between iron helms whenever the crystal chimes.

title: Greystone East Sally-Port
summary: Pumice-mortared basalt gatehouse scarred by demonic siege-catapult impacts.

p: Pumice-mortared basalt gatehouse scarred by demonic siege-catapult impacts.
Glowing slag-craters smoke across the glacis outside the iron bars.

title: Ashveil Summit Portal
summary: Narrow switchback stair carved into obsidian cliffs beneath a flickering rift-gate.

p: Narrow switchback stair carved into obsidian cliffs beneath a flickering rift-gate.
Violet sparks trail across charred grimoires abandoned on the steps.

title: The Unquenched Jaw
summary: Open magma-veined fissure straddling the western mana-cannon bastion.

p: Open magma-veined fissure straddling the western mana-cannon bastion.
White-hot slag spits from floor cracks beside chained iron anvils.

title: Magnetic Iron Narrows
summary: Thirty-pace defile cut straight through raw magnetic ore between spiked portcullises.

p: Thirty-pace defile cut straight through raw magnetic ore between spiked portcullises.
Iron scabbards tug sideways against the cliffs while crossbows click above.

title: Citadel Iron Drawbridge
summary: Six-inch-chained iron span suspended above a sluggish river of molten basalt.

p: Six-inch-chained iron span suspended above a sluggish river of molten basalt.
Murder-holes gape blackly above the gatehouse winches.

title: Three-Roads Watch
summary: Star-shaped ash-plain fort locking down all three approaches to the inner caldera.

p: Star-shaped ash-plain fort locking down all three approaches to the inner caldera.
Three converging dust plumes mark relief columns marching through soot.

title: The Threshold Nave
summary: Geometric obsidian hall dominated by twin doors of pale silver and weeping fire.

p: Geometric obsidian hall dominated by twin doors of pale silver and weeping fire.
Headless statues stand silent vigil beside the cooling Anchor Seals.

title: Alder Ferry Pier
summary: Splintered cedar pilings jutting into the gray current where flat-bottomed barges once crossed.

p: Splintered cedar pilings jutting into the gray current where flat-bottomed barges once crossed.
Snapped tow-ropes dangle into the eddies beside an overturned toll-chest.

title: Collapsed Brier Watchtower
summary: A listing timber signal-post choked by thorny vines above the eastern wagon track.

p: A listing timber signal-post choked by thorny vines above the eastern wagon track.
Fletched border arrows still bristle from the charred roof beams.

title: Garrick's Mill-Sluice
summary: A moss-slick stone weir holding back a stagnant millpond clogged with dead reeds.

p: A moss-slick stone weir holding back a stagnant millpond clogged with dead reeds.
The iron sluice-wheel is chained shut, backing foul water over the road.

title: Cairn of Three Spears
summary: A wind-scoured mound of river cobbles marking an ancient truce between border clans.

p: A wind-scoured mound of river cobbles marking an ancient truce between border clans.
Three rusted spearheads jut from the cairn's crown like crooked teeth.

title: Saint Oswin's Wayshrine
summary: A leaning sandstone niche housing a faceless statue draped in wet woolen ribbons.

p: A leaning sandstone niche housing a faceless statue draped in wet woolen ribbons.
Half-burned tallow stubs float in the rainwater pooling at the saint's feet.

title: Old Tanner's Hollow
summary: Sunken lime-pits and collapsed drying racks hidden inside a damp willow copse.

p: Sunken lime-pits and collapsed drying racks hidden inside a damp willow copse.
The sour reek of curing hides lingers beneath freshly turned earth.

title: Shattered Axle Crossing
summary: A shallow gravel bar littered with splintered oak spokes and waterlogged grain sacks.

p: A shallow gravel bar littered with splintered oak spokes and waterlogged grain sacks.
Deep bootprints lead straight from the wrecked supply wagon into the brush.

title: The Crooked Willow
summary: A gnarled riverside tree whose lowest bough bears frayed hemp nooses over the mud.

p: A gnarled riverside tree whose lowest bough bears frayed hemp nooses over the mud.
Crows scatter from the branches, leaving behind brass buttons in the silt.

title: Redbank Flint Pit
summary: Stepped chalk excavations where border knappers once mined spark-stone for garrison tinderboxes.

p: Stepped chalk excavations where border knappers once mined spark-stone for garrison tinderboxes.
Abandoned iron picks lie rusting beside piles of sharp, freshly split chert.

title: Flooded Tithe-Granary
summary: A squat brick storehouse tilted half into the riverbank after last autumn's surge.

p: A squat brick storehouse tilted half into the riverbank after last autumn's surge.
Sprouting barley spills through a cracked cellar grate into the black mud.

title: Smoldering Peat Kilns
summary: Domed brick ovens sunken into the bog, venting thin tendrils of acrid yellow smoke.

p: Domed brick ovens sunken into the bog, venting thin tendrils of acrid yellow smoke.
Charred wheelbarrows sit abandoned beside stacks of black turf bricks.

title: The Drowned Belfry
summary: Only the stone steeple of an old parish chapel rises above the stagnant red water.

p: Only the stone steeple of an old parish chapel rises above the stagnant red water.
A cracked bronze bell sways slightly whenever marsh gas bubbles up below.

title: Stilt-Hut of Bog-Mire
summary: A leaning reed shack perched on rotting cypress poles above a scum-covered pool.

p: A leaning reed shack perched on rotting cypress poles above a scum-covered pool.
Glass jars filled with dark, writhing shapes hang from the eaves.

title: The Rib-Bone Causeway
summary: A narrow footpath paved with bleached animal ribs and split logs across bottomless mire.

p: A narrow footpath paved with bleached animal ribs and split logs across bottomless mire.
Every step sinks an inch, squelching black water over the ancient bones.

title: Sunken Siege-Battery
summary: Rotted timber platforms holding two half-submerged trebuchets from a forgotten rebellion.

p: Rotted timber platforms holding two half-submerged trebuchets from a forgotten rebellion.
Sling-ropes hang like dead vines above crates of moss-covered stone shot.

title: Weeping Alder Thicket
summary: Twisted bog-trees dripping amber sap into dark pools choked with crimson duckweed.

p: Twisted bog-trees dripping amber sap into dark pools choked with crimson duckweed.
Tattered scraps of pilgrim cloth flutter from the lowest thorns.

title: The Quicklime Trench
summary: A long, sunken ditch crusted with white lime along the edge of the eastern dike.

p: A long, sunken ditch crusted with white lime along the edge of the eastern dike.
Broken wooden shovels jut from the crust like crooked grave markers.

title: False-Light Beacon
summary: An iron cage mounted on a crooked pole where pale marsh-lights gather after dusk.

p: An iron cage mounted on a crooked pole where pale marsh-lights gather after dusk.
Skeletal hands still clutch the base of the post beneath a foot of peat.

title: Mire-Cult Stone
summary: A flat slab of black basalt carved with spiral channels stained dark with dried blood.

p: A flat slab of black basalt carved with spiral channels stained dark with dried blood.
Woven reed idols sit in a ring around a bowl of foul bog-water.

title: The Beached Fen-Barge
summary: The mossy hull of a flat-bottomed troop transport wedged firmly into a peat hummock.

p: The mossy hull of a flat-bottomed troop transport wedged firmly into a peat hummock.
Rusted shields still hang along the gunwales above a flooded cargo hold.

title: Cracked Brine Pans
summary: Terraced stone basins along the tidal flats crusted with dirty gray sea-salt.

p: Terraced stone basins along the tidal flats crusted with dirty gray sea-salt.
Wooden rakes lie snapped beside mounds of uncollected salt crystals.

title: Leviathan Jaw-Gate
summary: Two colossal sun-bleached rib bones lashed together over a narrow cliffside smugglers' path.

p: Two colossal sun-bleached rib bones lashed together over a narrow cliffside smugglers' path.
Salt wind whistles through carved sailor-marks etched into the bone.

title: Blind-Beacon Tower
summary: A salt-eaten stone lighthouse whose bronze mirror was smashed out during a corsair raid.

p: A salt-eaten stone lighthouse whose bronze mirror was smashed out during a corsair raid.
Cold ash fills the fire-pan while gull nests choke the spiral stairs.

title: The Splintered Cove
summary: A jagged reef impaling the broken hulls of three royal patrol galleys.

p: A jagged reef impaling the broken hulls of three royal patrol galleys.
Barnacle-covered oars wash back and forth in the red-stained surf.

title: Harbor Chain-Winch
summary: A squat capstan house holding one end of a rusted harbor-blocking iron chain.

p: A squat capstan house holding one end of a rusted harbor-blocking iron chain.
Thick links trail straight down into the crashing waves like a sea-serpent.

title: Tide-Hollow Grotto
summary: A basalt cavern accessible only at low water, stacked with tarred brandy casks.

p: A basalt cavern accessible only at low water, stacked with tarred brandy casks.
Wet bootprints lead deeper into the dark behind a false wall of driftwood.

title: Mariner's Cliff-Niche
summary: Shallow caves cut into the sea-cliff where drowned sailors' skulls rest behind iron grilles.

p: Shallow caves cut into the sea-cliff where drowned sailors' skulls rest behind iron grilles.
Salt-crusted copper coins glint inside empty eye sockets.

title: Sea-Cliff Anchor Smithy
summary: An open-air stone hearth battered by spray, flanked by half-forged iron flukes.

p: An open-air stone hearth battered by spray, flanked by half-forged iron flukes.
A massive cracked anvil sits tilted in the wet shingle.

title: The Abyssal Tide-Pool
summary: A deep circular sinkhole in the coastal rock that churns violently even in calm weather.

p: A deep circular sinkhole in the coastal rock that churns violently even in calm weather.
Carved stone steps descend straight into the black, foaming water.

title: False-Harbor Gallows
summary: A tall timber crane perched on a jagged headland to lure merchant ships onto the rocks.

p: A tall timber crane perched on a jagged headland to lure merchant ships onto the rocks.
Shattered cargo crates and bleached ribs litter the coves directly below.

title: The Ash-Choked Viaduct
summary: A towering stone aqueduct whose dry channel is packed three feet deep with gray soot.

p: A towering stone aqueduct whose dry channel is packed three feet deep with gray soot.
Scorched royal banners hang limp from the arches over the barren plain.

title: The Blackened Groves
summary: Rows of petrified apple trees turned to charcoal by rolling ember-winds from the capital.

p: Rows of petrified apple trees turned to charcoal by rolling ember-winds from the capital.
Brittle branches snap like dry bones underfoot in the dead silence.

title: Royal Gunpowder Foundry
summary: A blackened stone manufactory ringed by slag heaps and shattered bronze cannon molds.

p: A blackened stone manufactory ringed by slag heaps and shattered bronze cannon molds.
Sulfur dust coats the floor beside half-filled barrels of coarse black powder.

title: The Iron-Cage Crossroads
summary: Tall iron gibbets creaking in the hot wind along the main highway to the inner walls.

p: Tall iron gibbets creaking in the hot wind along the main highway to the inner walls.
Charred parchment decrees remain nailed to the stone base of each post.

title: Square of the Molten Bell
summary: A cracked marble plaza dominated by a massive cathedral bell fused into a lump of bronze.

p: A cracked marble plaza dominated by a massive cathedral bell fused into a lump of bronze.
Vitrified cobbles mark where crown-fire rained down during the purge.

title: The Soot-Sealed Cistern
summary: A domed brick reservoir whose iron hatch was welded shut to keep ash from fouling the water.

p: A domed brick reservoir whose iron hatch was welded shut to keep ash from fouling the water.
Scratch marks cover the bronze door where desperate hands tried to pry it open.

title: Scorched Watch-Bastion
summary: A soot-stained fortress gatehouse flanked by cold iron braziers ten feet wide.

p: A soot-stained fortress gatehouse flanked by cold iron braziers ten feet wide.
Rows of blackened halberds stand neatly racked beside piles of fused armor.

title: The Cindered Chancellery
summary: Gutted marble halls where thousands of tax rolls and noble pedigrees burned to black flakes.

p: Gutted marble halls where thousands of tax rolls and noble pedigrees burned to black flakes.
A single iron strongbox sits untouched amid knee-deep drifts of paper ash.

title: Ember-Glass Quarry
summary: Jagged pits of black volcanic glass mined to tip the spears of the royal vanguard.

p: Jagged pits of black volcanic glass mined to tip the spears of the royal vanguard.
Razor-sharp splinters glint across the churned earth like fallen stars.

title: The Cinder Causeway
summary: A wide basalt road lined with headless statues leading directly toward the smoking citadel.

p: A wide basalt road lined with headless statues leading directly toward the smoking citadel.
Hot cinders drift across the paving stones like dying fireflies.

title: Watchman Joren
summary: Act I gate-sentry stationed along the southern frontier approaches, watching the foggy road toward Ashbrook.

p: A gaunt border militiaman in a dented kettle-helm with soot smeared across both cheeks.
Carries: A notched halberd and a cracked horn lantern.

list: Keep low by the gatehouse—their archers have the cobbled lane ranged to the inch.
Gate timbers are holding, barely. Tell Garrick we need iron wedges.

p: Joren has spent six wet months squinting into the drizzle from a leaking wooden box, counting supply carts that never return. He trusts hot tallow, dry bowstrings, and very little else.

title: Clerk Oswin
summary: Act I tax-clerk stationed near the Alder River crossings, keeping stubborn track of border tariffs and chains.

p: A shivering middle-aged scribe clutching a wet wool cloak over ink-stained fingers.
Carries: A brass-bound tally slate and a broken padlock.

list: Three months of river tariffs sank in that ditch! Don't let the gnolls chew the box.
If the silver's gone, Thornwick's militia won't stay past sundown.

p: Even with gnolls howling across the shallows, Clerk Oswin refuses to close his inkpot until every wagon's weight is entered in the daybook. Border soldiers mock him, yet he always knows who passed through last.

title: Peat-Cutter Mara
summary: Act I bog guide working the soggy Fenwick turf-ditches, familiar with every safe plank and mire-pocket.

p: A wiry woman wrapped in greased horsehide with mud dried up to her thighs.
Carries: A long iron-shod peat spade.

list: Step only on the black tussocks—green moss hides sinkholes deep enough to swallow a horse.
Keep your torches hooded; bog-lights draw things with teeth.

p: Mara reads dark water the way city clerks read vellum, spotting sunken cart-tracks and wisp-traps twenty paces ahead. She carries a long iron-shod turf spade that doubles nicely as a polearm.

title: Runner Talia
summary: Act I frontier scout carrying dispatches between Thornwick, Craghorn Ridge, and Ravenwatch Keep.

p: A breathless young outrider with a blood-soaked bandage wrapped around her left calf.
Carries: An empty leather dispatch tube.

list: The bone totems in the pines are feeding their wards—burn them before night falls!
My leg won't carry me back up the ridge, so make every arrow count.

p: Talia travels light with two dry pairs of wool socks and a brass whistle looped around her neck. She knows every goat-track off the main highway, which is the only reason she is still breathing.

title: Sawyer Dobb
summary: Act I lumberjack working the Greywood timber camps, supplying palisade logs and planks for Thornwick.

p: A broad-shouldered woodcutter missing two fingers, wearing a sawdust-caked leather apron.
Carries: A two-man crosscut saw slung over one shoulder.

list: Tarn's turncoats locked our best iron axes inside the central timber shed.
Burn their pork barrels, just leave the seasoned oak planks intact.

p: Dobb smells permanently of fresh pine resin and wet sawdust, with forearms thick as mill-axles. He has little patience for southern bailiffs who confiscate his best oak beams while leaving the local roof leaking.

title: Warden Hale
summary: Act II outpost-scout patrolling the Redmarsh trails, keeping watch on canyon passes and desert markers.

p: A sun-darkened ranger in salt-stiffened rawhide with a cracked spyglass hung at his neck.
Carries: A curved horn-bow and a bundle of signal flags.

list: Dust storms roll off the basin without warning—keep horns close or lose half your column.
The ridge blinds are clear for now, though raiders still prowl the dry arroyos.

p: Transferred south when the northern line thinned, Hale traded his wool cloak for vinegar-cured linen and a scarred canteen. He speaks rarely, wastes no water, and checks every horizon twice before moving.

title: Miner Tomas
summary: Act II quarry foreman overseeing the stepped basalt terraces and timber pit-props of the Deep Quarry.

p: A stocky quarryman covered in black ironstone dust with raw chain-chafes around his wrists.
Carries: A heavy steel quarry-pick.

list: Break the slave-pen locks on the middle terrace and three hundred picks join your line!
Gorrathul's overseers hid the hoist keys in the pit—bury them.

p: Grey ironstone dust sits permanently in the creases around Tomas's eyes. He knows the exact groan a ceiling beam makes ten seconds before a collapse, and he guards his crew's tools like silver.

title: Drover Vane
summary: Act II caravan teamster hauling freight across the treacherous salt-pans and corduroy roads of Redmarsh.

p: A one-eyed caravan driver with cracked lips and a salt-crusted felt hat.
Carries: A braided rawhide mule-whip.

list: My lead mules bolted when the sand-raiders whistled—help me haul these crates off the flats!
Never trust a dry creek bed at noon; lurkers sleep two inches under the crust.

p: Drover Vane curses his mules with affectionate precision and keeps two spare axles lashed beneath every wagon bed. Anyone who has dragged salt-pork through alkali mud without losing a wheel earns respect.

title: Surveyor Nira
summary: Act II field geomancer monitoring the fractured quartz obelisks and static storms of the high plateau.

p: An indigo-robed scholar squinting through smoked-quartz spectacles against blowing grit.
Carries: A brass plumb-bob and charcoal rubbing-pad.

list: The quartz spire is cracking! Kill the blood-chanters before the static cooks us alive!
Keep those rubbings dry—Zahra will need every glyph on that parchment.

p: Nira carries a satchel full of copper wire, plumb-bobs, and cracked chalk-slates, measuring ley-drift while sand whips across her spectacles. She blames sloppy southern maintenance for every storm on the flats.

title: Sentry Kell
summary: Act II well-guard stationed along the desert watering posts, protecting scarce aquifers from raiders and taint.

p: A hollow-cheeked pikeman leaning heavily on a spear beside a chained iron well-cover.
Carries: A battered copper ladle.

list: One drop of beetle-bile ruins a whole cistern—keep those scourges off the stone rim!
Water's rationed to half a pint till Bram's wagons reach the gate.

p: Kell stands ten-hour shifts beside brackish stone troughs with a loaded crossbow resting across his knees. In Redmarsh, guarding clean water makes you more popular than a priest and twice as likely to be shot.

title: Corporal Brenn
summary: Act III marine non-commissioned officer holding the wet coastal approaches and shingle spits near Oakhaven.

p: A salt-cured infantry corporal in a rusted breastplate with seaweed tangled in his greaves.
Carries: A notched boarding-axe.

list: Watch the tide-lines—heavy mail sinks like an anchor when the surf rolls over the spit!
Hold the plank-walk; Oakhaven's marines are right behind you.

p: Corporal Brenn barks orders loud enough to carry over breaking surf and never lets a recruit sit down in wet boots. Three seasons of boarding actions left him with a crooked nose and iron discipline.

title: Pilot Maren
summary: Act III coastal navigator guiding evacuation vessels through fogbanks, boom-chains, and jagged shingle reefs.

p: A weather-beaten coast pilot in oiled yellow canvas with brass dividers tucked in his sash.
Carries: A salt-stained sounding lead and line.

list: You have two hours before spring tide floods the lower ward—move fast or drown in plate!
Keep off the kelp-slick steps; one slip drops you straight into the sluice.

p: Maren knows every hidden rock and rip-tide between Oakhaven and the Western Rim by the color of the foam alone. Ship-captains who ignore her hand-signals usually end up swimming back to shore.

title: Apothecary Linn
summary: Act III field medic tending wounded borderers and refugees along the coastal roads and chapel infirmaries.

p: A pale apprentice surgeon in a vinegar-soaked apron with blood dried under her fingernails.
Carries: A wicker tray of boiled linen rolls.

list: Keep those cleaver-happy raiders off the tent ropes—half our wounded can't even crawl!
Sera's loading the last stretchers now; hold the creek trail ten more minutes.

p: Apothecary Linn keeps her needles boiled in sour wine and her voice flat even when cannon shot rattles the roof tiles. She measures a battle not in banners captured, but in clean linen spent.

title: Lock-Keeper Orin
summary: Act III canal engineer maintaining the heavy sluice-gates and freshwater channels feeding Harborwatch.

p: A grease-stained canal mechanic with a swollen bruised shoulder and a heavy iron wrench.
Carries: A three-foot iron gear-wedge.

list: Drive these wedges into the center capstan before their sappers trip the floodgates!
Those gears won't turn again this winter—the east bridge is safe.

p: Orin wears tallow-stained coveralls and carries a heavy iron wrench tucked through his belt like a sword. He treats the twin floodgates like temperamental horses that only obey a firm hand.

title: Fire-Warden Cole
summary: Act III dock-captain coordinating fire-buckets, pitch stores, and seawall gun crews along the war-docks.

p: A soot-blackened dockworker coughing through a wet wool scarf tied over his nose.
Carries: A hooked fire-pike and sand bucket.

list: Pitch-pots are raining off Kael's flagship—clear the seawall stairs so we can douse the piers!
Save the drydocks first; without hulls, we never cross the southern straits.

p: Cole's eyebrows have been singed off twice fighting burning timber barges, yet he still refuses to leave the piers. Give him a bucket line and clear flagstones, and he will hold back an inferno.

title: Ash-Scout Riven
summary: Act IV highland pathfinder charting safe basalt trails through the sulfur fissures and cinder-snow of the caldera.

p: A lean vanguard scout in soot-grey leather with smoked-glass goggles pushed onto his forehead.
Carries: A bundle of white-chalked warning stakes.

list: Stay off the yellow crust—boiling sulfur sits two inches beneath that brittle shell!
Highcrest bluff is clear, though the ash-storms are thickening to the east.

p: Riven wraps wet linen around his nose and tests every smooth ash-drift with a six-foot ironwood pole before stepping forward. Few scouts survive a week near Highcrest without developing his quiet paranoia.

title: Sapper Garr
summary: Act IV demolitionist specializing in breaching basalt walls, grounding spires, and sabotaging enemy magazines.

p: A squat, burn-scarred engineer wearing thick leather welding gauntlets and an iron visor.
Carries: A keg of black prism-powder.

list: Cover my team while we set the charges on the West Conduit—one spark ends us early!
Charges are primed; clear the dais before the stone splits.

p: Garr smells permanently of sulfur, blasting powder, and scorched leather, and he grins widest when a wall starts leaning. Regular infantry give him ten paces of elbow room whenever he opens his pack.

title: Watchman Varo
summary: Act IV wall-guard holding the battered pumice-mortar battlements of Greystone Bastion against Iron Pact sieges.

p: A exhausted Greystone defender in cracked basalt-dusted plate with a sling on his left arm.
Carries: A heavy steel windlass crossbow.

list: Three demonic catapults are chewing our east parapet to gravel—sally out and burn them!
Parapet's patched with pumice mortar, though my ears are still ringing.

p: Watchman Varo sleeps sitting upright with his helmet strapped on, waking instantly whenever siege-golem footsteps vibrate through the stone. He has lost count of the assaults, yet his pike-point stays sharp.

title: Penitent Sola
summary: Act IV ash-marked archivist keeping solemn record of the ancient inscriptions and seals near the caldera heart.

p: A barefoot ash-robed witness carrying a chain of tarnished brass name-plates.
Carries: A small iron censer smoking with grey ash.

list: Speak softly in the nave—the First Watch still stands bound to those obsidian pillars.
Two doors, two prices. Choose which temperature you want for Thornvael.

p: Sola traded her abbey robes for scorched wool and a brass rubbing-box, determined that someone should remember what stood beneath the mountain before the fire takes it. Her hands are stained black with charcoal.

title: Stoker Brann
summary: Act IV smith-mate tending the roaring volcanic bellows and slag-troughs of Ironcamp's forward forge-yards.

p: A shirtless, keloid-scarred forge-hand wearing a heavy asbestos-lined leather apron.
Carries: Long iron crucible tongs.

list: Vok needs slag-billets from the lower vents before we can re-temper your vanguard's shields!
Keep your steel oiled; volcanic fumes pit bare iron in half an hour.

p: Brann works stripped to a heavy leather apron even in freezing highland wind, shoveling glowing ironstone billets with tireless rhythm. He insists cold steel is just lazy metal waiting to be woken up.

title: Ferryman Garren
summary: Act I river ferryman operating the flatboats and rope-crossings along the rain-swollen Alder bends.

p: A stooped river-man in a tarred leather jerkin with rope-calloused hands and milky eyes.
Carries: A ten-foot ashwood punt-pole and a rusted tin bailer.

list: Bridge is out upstream, and the toll-brigands watch the shallow gravel. Pay a silver if you want dry knees.
Current's running strong today; keep your armor strapped tight in the skiff.

p: Hobb charges two coppers for a dry crossing and double if your horse kicks the gunwale. He has ferried tax bailiffs, smugglers, and gnoll-hunters alike without ever asking a single unnecessary question.

title: Peddler Merrin
summary: Act I wandering peddler hauling dry socks, flint, and salted eels along the muddy northern tracks.

p: A wiry trader bent beneath a towering wicker pack clanking with pots, tallow, and dried herbs.
Carries: A gnarled walking staff notched with mile-marks.

list: Even the highwaymen rarely rob a man carrying turnips and boot-grease—too heavy to run with!
Need spare bowstrings or oilskin? Better buy before you reach the fens.

p: Bram pushes a squeaking handcart straight through warzones because soldiers always pay better than farmers when their boots fall apart. He claims he has no politics beyond honest copper and dry roads.

title: Corporal Vane
summary: Act I former regular hiding along the willow banks after walking away from a Salt-Tithe enforcement column.

p: A hollow-cheeked pikeman missing one boot, wearing a muddy cloak with torn royal insignia.
Carries: A snapped pike-shaft used as a crutch.

list: They sent twenty of us to hold a flooded ditch without rations. I chose mud over a grave.
If you see Thornwick patrols, tell them Vane drowned at the ford.

p: Corporal Vane still wears his patched uniform coat with the brass Crown buttons ripped clean off. He insists he signed up to fight raiders, not to burn northern grain barns for southern clerks.

title: Mother Tilda
summary: Act I rural herbalist gathering willow-bark, bitter rue, and bog-moss along the damp river bluffs.

p: An elderly woman in a homespun shawl stained green at the cuffs from crushed river-mint.
Carries: A woven rush basket brimming with muddy roots.

list: Chew white willow bark when the river-chill gets in your joints—keeps the shaking fever off.
The reeds grow thicker every year where blood was spilled.

p: Mother Tilda has outlived three bailiffs and two border wars by knowing which weeds cure trench-fever and which ones sour a bully's stew. Even superstitious levies tip their caps when she passes.

title: Brother Aldous
summary: Act I traveling pilgrim of the Radiant Light walking the muddy shrine-roads between northern parishes.

p: A barefoot penitent wrapped in coarse burlap, his forehead smudged with gray river-ash.
Carries: A carved wooden rosary and a battered tin alms-bowl.

list: I walk the old border stones to pray for those who fell before the Compact broke.
No shrine stands untouched by greed, yet the stones still remember.

p: Brother Aldous carries a worn ash staff and a tin cup, stopping at every roadside boundary stone to brush away moss and say a quiet blessing. He refuses to hurry, even when wolves howl nearby.

title: Tinker Pip
summary: Act I itinerant tinker mending cracked kettles, loose rivets, and bent buckles near the river bridges.

p: A soot-speckled youth wearing spectacles mended with copper wire and a scorched leather apron.
Carries: A portable charcoal brazier and a ring of iron tongs.

list: Cracked kettle? Bent buckle? Give me ten minutes and a pinch of flux, good as forged!
I stay close to the crossroads—soldiers always break something.

p: Pip can patch a split leather strap or solder a leaking canteen in five minutes flat using nothing but a charcoal pot and wire scraps. Soldiers treat him better than most lieutenants.

title: Digger Marn
summary: Act II bog-edge peat-cutter harvesting fuel blocks along the damp transition into the Redmarsh flats.

p: A broad-shouldered bogman caked to the waist in black mud, squinting through a cloud of midges.
Carries: A long-handled iron turf-spade.

list: Dug up three rusted helmets and a pickled hand before noon. Redmarsh never lets go of anything.
Keep to the white-marked stakes unless you fancy sinking to your chin.

p: Digger Marn spends his days slicing black turf into neat bricks to dry in the harsh southern wind. He knows every sinkhole along the ditch and never trusts ground that looks too green.

title: Old Reed-Eyes
summary: Act II solitary hermit living in a stilted reed-hut on the brackish fringes of Redmarsh.

p: A skeletal recluse draped in woven sedge-mats, his beard tangled with dried duckweed.
Carries: A crooked driftwood crook hung with dried frog-skins.

list: Civilization rots faster than bog-oak. Out here, at least the monsters don't levy taxes.
The mire-heretics chant at midnight; plug your ears with beeswax.

p: Old Reed-Eyes stopped coming into town ten years ago after a tax clerk tried to assess his fishing net. He trades sharp warnings and dried marsh-herbs to travelers who remember to knock politely.

title: Master Corvus
summary: Act II traveling apothecary breeding alkali leeches and brewing bitter antitoxins for desert patrols.

p: A gaunt physician in a waxed oilcloth coat and a wide-brimmed hat stuffed with dried wormwood.
Carries: A wooden crate clinking with stoppered glass leech-jars.

list: Swamp-bloat kills more mercenaries than steel! My leeches draw the black humor right out.
Never scratch a bog-fly bite; rub it with bitter-root paste.

p: Master Corvus carries a wicker basket full of glass jars that slosh ominously whenever he walks. His remedies taste like boiled copper and vinegar, yet they pull viper venom out faster than prayer.

title: Surveyor Fenwick
summary: Act II frontier cartographer charting sinking embankments and shifting brine-channels across the wastes.

p: A mud-splattered scholar clutching a waterproof leather scroll-case against his chest.
Carries: A brass sighting-level and a knotted measuring cord.

list: Half the roads on the royal map sank three winters ago! I'm redrawing the dikes before another column drowns.
If you spot solid stone ruins, mark them for me—everything else is shifting peat.

p: Fenwick's ink-stained sleeves and brass dividers never leave his side, even when sand-raiders prowl the ridges. He insists a bad map kills more soldiers than a dull sword ever could.

title: Raker Nell
summary: Act II resourceful scavenger combing overturned supply wagons and alkali flats for salvageable iron.

p: A wiry woman in patched waders with a necklace of tarnished buckles and salvaged buttons.
Carries: A long wooden pole fitted with a three-pronged iron grapple.

list: You fight the ghouls, I fish their pockets out of the silt—fair division of labor, wouldn't you say?
Nothing's truly lost in Redmarsh if your grappling hook is long enough.

p: Raker Nell carries a long hooked pole and a burlap sack, prying intact buckles, horseshoes, and unbroken bottles out of the mud before the brine eats them. Nothing goes to waste on her watch.

title: Penitent Garr
summary: Act II wandering zealot preaching harsh penance along the sun-baked roads of Redmarsh.

p: A wild-eyed fanatic wearing a spiked iron collar over scarred, mud-streaked shoulders.
Carries: A knotted hemp scourge stained dark.

list: The Mire is our purgatory! Only through cold mud and bitter pain are our sins washed clean!
Do not strike the heretics with anger—pity their blindness!

p: Penitent Garr walks barefoot across salt-crust that blisters ordinary hides, muttering warnings about the coming heat. Caravan guards give him wide berth, though his grim prophecies rarely miss the mark.

title: Diver Sal
summary: Act III coastal salvager swimming out to shattered hulls wedged along the shingle reefs at low tide.

p: A barrel-chested coastal woman with salt-bleached hair and scars from barnacle cuts across both forearms.
Carries: A greased seal-bladder float and a heavy iron pry-bar.

list: Three royal pay-ships went down off these reefs last gale. Corsairs get the decks; I get the holds.
Watch the tide-pools—reef-stalkers nest under the rusted hulls.

p: Diver Sal holds her breath longer than any marine in Harborwatch and carries a weighted iron pry-bar strapped to her thigh. She knows the exact worth of brass ship-fittings and dry powder kegs.

title: Raker Orin
summary: Act III coastal salt-worker scraping coarse white crystals from tidal evaporation pans outside Oakhaven.

p: A sun-baked laborer with cracked lips, squinted eyes, and boots crusted white with dried brine.
Carries: A wide wooden salt-scraper.

list: Royal taxmen take nine bushels of salt out of ten, and leave us to fend off pirates with wooden rakes.
Fresh water's worth twice as much as grog along this stretch of cliff.

p: Raker Orin's hands are cracked white from brine and sun, yet his quiet labor keeps the evacuation fleet's beef barrels from rotting at sea. He watches the horizon more closely than any lookout.

title: Kaelo the Free
summary: Act III former galley-slave who broke his chains and swam ashore from the hostile blockade fleet.

p: A muscular man bearing raw iron-shackle scars on both wrists and a stolen corsair sash.
Carries: A broken galley-oar bound with iron bands.

list: Rowed for Draven's raiders four years before a reef cracked our keel. Never wearing chains again.
If you spot a slaver patrol, hit the whip-master first—the rest scatter.

p: Kaelo still wears a sawed-off iron cuff around his left ankle as a reminder never to surrender alive. He knows the blockade's patrol timings and gladly points coastal guns straight at his old captors.

title: Warden Mirella
summary: Act III coastal scout using trained sea-hawks to spot approaching raiders and blockade sails through fog.

p: A wind-worn ranger wrapped in gull-gray wool with a thick leather gauntlet reaching her elbow.
Carries: A hooded sea-hawk perched on a driftwood T-bar.

list: My bird spots corsair sails three leagues out. Right now, two longboats are hugging the southern cove.
Cliff-harpies hate falcons—keeps them off my perch, at least.

p: Warden Mirella wears a scarred rawhide gauntlet and whistles sharp notes that carry cleanly against the gale. Her birds see through coastal haze far better than any brass spyglass.

title: Old Barto
summary: Act III veteran fisherman repairing hemp nets and rigging ropes along Oakhaven's lower coves.

p: A hunchbacked sailor sitting on an upturned tar barrel, fingers flying through knotted hemp twine.
Carries: A bone netting-needle and a coil of tarred cord.

list: Used to haul silver cod by the ton. Now half the time we pull up drowned bones or barnacle-crabs.
Never cast a net near the Abyssal Pool unless you want something pulling back.

p: Old Barto's knees gave out years ago, yet his fingers still tie knots faster than a young marine can draw a knife. He listens quietly to every rumor drifting off the docks.

title: Keeper Torin
summary: Act III steadfast keeper tending the oil-lamps and brass reflectors of the coastal warning beacons.

p: A pale, gaunt old man smelling strongly of whale-oil and damp wool, squinting against the daylight.
Carries: A brass oil-can and a heavy ring of iron tower keys.

list: Without whale-oil for the beacon, ships pile onto the teeth every night—and wreckers cheer.
The sea takes everything we build; we just pile stones back up.

p: Keeper Torin smells permanently of whale oil and salt spray, climbing two hundred granite steps twice a night without complaint. As long as his wick burns, lost ships still have a chance.

title: Sweeper Dax
summary: Act IV highland laborer shoveling volcanic cinder off supply roads and fortress roofs near Ironcamp.

p: A coughing worker wrapped in gray rags with a wet cloth tied tightly over his nose and mouth.
Carries: A wide iron coal-shovel and a creaking wooden handcart.

list: They pay two coppers a barrow to clear cinders off the royal road. Still cheaper than hiring soldiers.
Don't kick the gray drifts—hot embers hide underneath for days.

p: Sweeper Dax laughs that his job never runs out of work, since the caldera dumps two fresh inches of grey grit every morning. Beneath the soot, he knows every hidden cellar door in camp.

title: Scribe Malen
summary: Act IV former Collegium archivist who marched inland to copy ancient Threshold texts before they burn.

p: A trembling former court clerk in singed velvet robes, clutching half-burned tax rolls to his chest.
Carries: A cracked inkhorn and a bundle of charred vellum.

list: When the Inquisitor ordered the archives burned, I ran with the real debt-ledgers. Now I'm a dead man walking.
Every noble in the capital owes blood-gold to the Cinder Throne.

p: Scribe Malen lost his faculty stipend for arguing with senior magisters over the Schism. Now he crouches behind basalt walls with a tin inkhorn, preserving forbidden history one shaky page at a time.

title: Sergeant Thorne
summary: Act IV battle-hardened veteran who walked away from the Iron Pact after seeing their ruthless tactics.

p: A scarred heavy infantryman in blackened plate with the royal crest hammered flat off his breastplate.
Carries: A notched tower shield and a dented water-canteen.

list: I served the Crown twenty years until they ordered us to torch our own granaries. Let the Sovereign choke on his ashes.
Pyre-knights fight blind inside those heavy helms—strike their knees.

p: Sergeant Thorne carries twenty years of frontier scars and a battered halberd stripped of its former banner. He fights quietly now, asking only for honest company and a clean death.

title: Sister Vesper
summary: Act IV highland healer treating sulfur burns, ash-cough, and siege wounds along the caldera approaches.

p: A soot-stained medic wearing scorched linen bandages around her forearms and a pouch of grease-pots.
Carries: A wooden mortar and a tin flask of goose-fat salve.

list: Crown-fire blisters through boiled leather in seconds. Rub mutton-tallow on your skin before you face them.
Water's scarcer than silver out here; don't waste a drop washing your face.

p: Sister Vesper mixes cooling clay poultices with melted alpine snow to soothe blistered skin. Soldiers joke that her bedside manner is colder than her salves, yet nobody argues when she patches them up.

title: Vex the Ash-Runner
summary: Act IV daring smuggler slipping rare star-iron and pre-schism trinkets out of contested caldera ruins.

p: A lean rogue in a reversible charcoal cloak with soot smeared deliberately across his brow.
Carries: A lead-lined lockbox slung over one shoulder.

list: Rich lords pay fortunes to sneak family heirlooms out of the capital before the whole city turns to slag.
Inquisitors search wagons, never ash-carts.

p: Vex knows every dry culvert and blind ledge between Highcrest and the Outer Rampart. He sells to anyone with hard crowns, insisting that relics do no good buried under fifty feet of lava.

title: Old Cinder-Tongue
summary: Act IV scorched seer wandering the volcanic bluffs, chanting riddles about the Crown and the Furnace.

p: A wild-haired old man in scorched rags pointing a blackened finger toward the smoking citadel.
Carries: A cracked bronze hand-bell without a clapper.

list: Gold melts, iron bends, flesh chars—only the ash remains equal under the Sovereign's sky!
Listen to the wind through the viaducts; it sings the requiem of kings!

p: Old Cinder-Tongue stared into a glowing fissure too long and came back speaking in broken verse about headless kings and iron thrones. Sentries toss him hardbread mostly to keep him from shouting at night.

title: Surveyor Hal
summary: Act 1 surveyor

p: A frostbitten boundary-clerk in a patched sheepskin coat, squinting through cracked brass spectacles.
Carries: A leather map-case and a bent plumb-line.

list: My apprentice bolted when the stone sentinels woke—grab that brass sighting glass before the snow hides it.
Not a scratch on the lens! Now Thornwick can draw an honest road map.

title: Foreman Durn
summary: Act 1 quarry-foreman

p: A broad-shouldered dwarven shift-boss with coal-grimed knuckles and a notched iron pick-helve.
Carries: A dented brass shift-whistle and a copper-bound tally board.

list: Cultists locked the shift-office before we could haul out the paychest. Cut the warden down and crack that door.
Every silver bit accounted for. The crew remembers who kept their wages out of cultist hands.
